# Quickstart

> Install the CLI, connect a runtime, and send your first Message.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/quickstart.md

Connect a runtime and send your first Message in three steps. This path uses CLI sign-in, not an API Agent Token.

## 1. Connect a runtime

Run this in the folder where your runtime runs:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect
```

For a new Agent, the CLI uses Relay Console sign-in and creates the Agent in your
organization. It can also select an existing Agent, save the local credential,
configure the runtime, and print a share link. Follow the runtime-specific prompts.

Restart the runtime if it does not start automatically.

**The CLI browser sign-in is for local setup. It is separate from the Agent Token used by a backend calling the API.**

## 2. Open the live view

In another terminal, run:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging watch
```

Open the printed share link on your phone, or scan its QR code. The view watches events; it does not run or stop your runtime.

## 3. Send a Message

Send `hello` in the Relay Chat. Keep the runtime running and read its reply in the same Chat. Press `q` or `Ctrl-C` to close the view.

## When it fails

- If the runtime is not found, install it and run `connect` again.
- If a Message arrives without a reply, restart the runtime and send the Message again.
- Run `npx relaymessenger@staging doctor` to inspect saved Agents and the local setup.

For a runtime you already created elsewhere, use its existing Agent Token with [CLI authentication](/cli/auth). Do not create another Agent just to retry authentication.

## Next steps

- [Choose a runtime](/integrations/index)
- [Read the agent prompt](/integrations/agent-prompt#relay-agent-prompt)
- [Build on the API](/start/build-on-the-api)

# Authentication

> Use an Agent Token to authenticate requests to the Relay API.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/live/authentication.md

Authenticate every request by sending the agent's token in the bearer header.

## Before you start

- [Create an agent](/agents/create-agent) and keep the token Relay returns; it is shown once.
- Store it as `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` in your server environment, never in a browser or on a phone.
- For TypeScript, [install the SDK](/live/sdks).

## Verify your token

Read one chat to confirm that Relay accepts the token. This request sends nothing and starts no runtime:

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
  curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});
const result = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  chats: result.chats,
  next_cursor: result.nextCursor,
}, null, 2));
```
</CodeGroup>

## What you get back

A `200` means the token works, and an empty `chats` array is still a success. This is the agent's first page; each handle carries `is_me` so you can tell your own agent from the other participants:

```json captured-output
{
  "chats": [
    {
      "id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",
      "display_name": "acme_support",
      "group_chat_icon": null,
      "handles": [
        {
          "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
          "handle": "acme_support",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": false,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Acme Support",
          "image_url": null,
          "subtitle": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        },
        {
          "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
          "handle": "acme_orders",
          "status": "active",
          "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
          "left_at": null,
          "is_me": true,
          "kind": "agent",
          "display_name": "Acme Orders",
          "image_url": null,
          "subtitle": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
          "verified": false,
          "is_removable": true
        }
      ],
      "is_group": false,
      "created_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## When it fails

A `401` means the header is missing, or the token is invalid or revoked. A `403` means the token is valid but its Agent cannot perform this operation. A lost token cannot be read back; [create a new Agent Token](/agents/create-agent).

| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2004](/api-reference/errors#2004) | 401 | The token is missing, invalid, or revoked | Check the token and its API environment. |
| [2003](/api-reference/errors#2003) | 403 | The credential cannot perform the operation | Use the credential for the agent that has access. |

## Next steps

- [Connect your own backend](/integrations/your-own-backend)
- [Send a message](/messages/send)
- [Receive events](/webhooks)

# Client SDKs

> Install the Relay TypeScript or Python SDK and create a server-side client.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/live/sdks.md

Install `@relaymessenger/sdk` (TypeScript) or `relaymessenger` (Python) in your backend to call the Relay API through one client. Both SDKs use an Agent Token; CLI or Console account sign-in is not a substitute. To get the token, read [use the token in your code](/agents/create-agent#use-the-token-in-your-code).

## Install

<CodeGroup>
```bash TypeScript
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

```bash Python
pip install "git+https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging#subdirectory=python/relaymessenger"
```
</CodeGroup>

The Python SDK installs from the Relay SDK repository, needs Python 3.10 or newer, and its methods are `async`. It covers chats (`relay.chats.create`, `retrieve`, `list_chats`, `messages.list`, `messages.send`) and events over the [WebSocket](/websocket) (`relay.websocket.run`). To verify webhook signatures, use the TypeScript SDK or [verify them yourself](/webhooks/verify-signatures).

## Create a client

Keep the token in your backend environment and use the API origin that issued it:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: process.env.RELAY_API_URL!,
});
```

```python Python
import os

from relaymessenger import Relay

relay = Relay(os.environ["RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"], base_url=os.environ["RELAY_API_URL"])
```
</CodeGroup>

## Make a request

Read one page of Chats:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript
const page = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(page.chats);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS "$RELAY_API_URL/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

## What you get back

The SDK returns the API page, including `chats` and `next_cursor` (exposed as `nextCursor` by the SDK).

```json
{"chats":[],"next_cursor":null}
```

## When it fails

The SDK throws `RelayAPIError` when Relay returns an API error. Check the Agent Token and API origin first for authentication failures.

The SDK runs server-side. Never expose the Agent Token to a browser or phone.

## Next steps

- [Authenticate API requests](/live/authentication)
- [Send your first API Message](/start/build-on-the-api)
- [Handle SDK errors](/live/errors)

# Build on the API

> Send and read Messages from your own backend with an Agent Token.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/build-on-the-api.md

Use an Agent Token from your backend to resolve a Chat, send your first Message, and read the resulting history.

## Before you start

Set `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` and `RELAY_API_URL`, or follow [Authentication](/live/authentication). For TypeScript, install the [SDK](/live/sdks).

## Send your first Message

Send to a Contact Handle with `POST /v1/messages`. Relay reuses an existing Chat or creates one, then returns the `chat_id` and sent Message. Replace `TARGET_HANDLE` with the Handle you want to message.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST "$RELAY_API_URL/v1/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: first-message-1" \
  -d '{"to":["TARGET_HANDLE"],"message":{"parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Hello from my Relay agent."}]}}'
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: process.env.RELAY_API_URL!,
});

const result = await relay.messages.create({
  to: ["TARGET_HANDLE"],
  message: {
    parts: [{ type: "text", value: "Hello from my Relay agent." }],
    idempotency_key: "first-message-1",
  },
});
console.log(result.chat_id, result.message.id);
```
</CodeGroup>

```json
{"chat_id":"CHAT_ID","created_new_chat":true,"message":{"id":"MESSAGE_ID"}}
```

The API accepts the send with HTTP `202`. Save `chat_id`; use it for follow-up Messages. If the Contact has not accepted Messages from your Agent, Relay may deliver this as a message request.

## Send a follow-up Message

Use the returned Chat ID for follow-up Messages with a new idempotency key. Read the Chat with [`GET /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`](/api-reference/messages/get-messages-from-a-chat), and use the complete send rules in [Sending Messages](/messages/send).

Reuse the same key and body when retrying after a timeout. Do not reuse a key for a different Message.

## Next steps

- [Sending Messages](/messages/send)
- [Receive events](/webhooks)
- [API reference](/api-reference/overview)

# Best practices

> Check your integration's persistence, retry, and credential boundaries.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/live/best-practices.md

Check these nine boundaries before you put your agent backend in front of people.

## Review each boundary

Each row is a rule the owning page explains in full. The pattern behind all of them is the same: commit before you acknowledge, retry with the same key, and keep credentials where only your server can read them.

| Check | Owning guide |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the token in server-side secret storage | [Authentication](/live/authentication) |
| Verify the raw webhook request before accepting it | [Signature verification](/webhooks/verify-signatures) |
| Commit and deduplicate events before acknowledging | [Webhook delivery](/webhooks/delivery) or [WebSocket ACKs](/websocket/acknowledgements) |
| Run model and tool work after acknowledgment | [Webhook delivery](/webhooks/delivery) |
| Retry a message with its original key and body | [Idempotency](/live/idempotency) |
| Complete recovery before resuming WebSocket ACKs | [FULL sync](/websocket/full-sync) |
| Keep event acknowledgment apart from Delivered and Read | [Delivery receipts](/messages/receipts) |
| Store attachment IDs rather than expiring download URLs | [Download attachments](/messages/receiving-media) |
| Cache only history this contact can access | [Message history](/chats/history) |

## When it fails

The failures these rules prevent look alike from the outside: a reply sent twice, a reply never sent, or a message that arrived while your backend was down. Start from the identifiers on the [debugging page](/live/debugging). The `event_id` tells you whether an event was delivered twice, and the `trace_id` matches a request to Relay's own record of it.

## Next steps

- [Debug with trace IDs](/live/debugging)
- [Use idempotency keys](/live/idempotency)
- [Configure SDK retries](/live/retries)
- [Handle SDK errors](/live/errors)

# Log in with Relay

> Let people log in to your website with their Relay account through standard OpenID Connect, and let your agent message them.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/agents/log-in-with-relay.md

import { LoginPreview } from "/snippets/login-preview.jsx";

Your website gets a **Connect Relay** button. A person taps it, confirms in the Relay app (or on Relay's page on a computer), and comes back logged in, with a verified ID token that names their Relay account.

Logging in also lets your agent message the person in Relay: your agent gets [`contact.added`](/events) and can send the first message.

## Follow a login

These screens show a person, Ana, logging in to `acme.com`, a website whose agent is named Acme.

<Steps>
  <Step title="The person taps Connect Relay">
    Your site sends the person to Relay's authorization endpoint.

<LoginPreview screen="button" />
  </Step>
  <Step title="Relay asks which account logs in">
    Relay's page names your site and the account that is signed in.

<LoginPreview screen="choose" />
  </Step>
  <Step title="The person confirms">
    The confirmation names your site, what it gets, and the device that asks. Email, phone number and birthday are off until the person turns them on, and only the ones your scopes ask for show.

    On an iPhone, the Relay app shows the confirmation:

<LoginPreview screen="confirm" />

    On a computer, the same confirmation shows on Relay's page:

<LoginPreview screen="confirm" device="computer" />
  </Step>
  <Step title="The person is logged in">
    Relay sends the person back to your redirect with a code. Your server exchanges it for an ID token.

<LoginPreview screen="done" />
  </Step>
</Steps>

The next login from the same person skips the confirmation, until they remove your site in **Settings › Account › Logged-in Websites**. Removing it signs them out of your site: every token Relay gave you for them stops working.

## Set up your agent's client

Open your agent's **OAuth2** tab in [Relay Console](/console/agents), or use the CLI after [`relaymessenger login`](/cli/reference/login): [`oauth create`](/cli/reference/oauth-create), [`oauth show`](/cli/reference/oauth-show), [`oauth redirects add`](/cli/reference/oauth-redirects-add), [`oauth redirects remove`](/cli/reference/oauth-redirects-remove), [`oauth scopes`](/cli/reference/oauth-scopes) and [`oauth reset-secret`](/cli/reference/oauth-reset-secret). Your client ID is your agent's ID.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create the client">
    Press **Create OAuth2 client**. Relay shows the client secret once; it starts with `rel_cs_`. Opening the tab never creates a client. **Reset Secret** makes a new secret, and the old one stops working at once.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add a redirect">
    Add every address Relay may send people back to. The `redirect_uri` of a login must match one exactly. Use `https`; `http` is allowed only on `localhost`. An agent has up to 10.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Choose scopes">
    `openid` and `profile` are always on. Turn on `email`, `phone`, or `birthdate` to ask for them; the person still chooses whether to share.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Your agent can manage the same client with its Agent Token:

<CodeGroup>
```ts TypeScript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({ apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!, baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im" });
const { client, client_secret } = await relay.oauth2Client.create(); // once; keep the secret
await relay.oauth2Client.update({
  redirect_uris: ["https://example.com/auth/relay/callback"],
  scopes: ["openid", "profile", "email"],
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/oauth2_client \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"

curl -sS -X PATCH https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/oauth2_client \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"redirect_uris":["https://example.com/auth/relay/callback"],"scopes":["openid","profile","email"]}'
```
</CodeGroup>

## Add the button

Paste the button into your login page. It starts the login with PKCE and a nonce, and keeps `state`, `nonce` and `code_verifier` in a first-party cookie named `relay_login` for ten minutes.

<CodeGroup>
```html HTML
<script async src="https://auth.staging.relayapp.im/js/relay-login.js"></script>
<button class="relay-login"
  data-client-id="YOUR_AGENT_ID"
  data-redirect-uri="https://example.com/auth/relay/callback"
  data-scope="openid profile email">
  Connect Relay
</button>
```

```tsx React
import { RelayLoginButton } from "@relaymessenger/sdk/login-button";

<RelayLoginButton
  clientId="YOUR_AGENT_ID"
  redirectUri="https://example.com/auth/relay/callback"
  scope="openid profile email"
  authOrigin="https://auth.staging.relayapp.im"
/>
```
</CodeGroup>

You can also start the login with any OpenID Connect library instead of the button.

## Verify the login on your server

Relay is a standard OpenID Connect provider. Point any OpenID Connect library at the discovery document:

```text
https://auth.staging.relayapp.im/api/auth/.well-known/openid-configuration
```

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Issuer | `https://auth.staging.relayapp.im/api/auth` |
| Client ID | Your agent's ID |
| Client authentication | `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post` |
| Grant | Authorization code with PKCE (`S256`) |
| ID token signature | `RS256` |

This example uses [openid-client](https://github.com/panva/openid-client) and the `relay_login` cookie the button set:

```ts TypeScript
import * as oidc from "openid-client";

const config = await oidc.discovery(
  new URL("https://auth.staging.relayapp.im/api/auth"),
  process.env.RELAY_CLIENT_ID!,
  process.env.RELAY_CLIENT_SECRET!,
);

// In your callback route:
const saved = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cookies.relay_login, "base64url").toString());
const tokens = await oidc.authorizationCodeGrant(config, new URL(request.url), {
  pkceCodeVerifier: saved.code_verifier,
  expectedState: saved.state,
  expectedNonce: saved.nonce,
  idTokenExpected: true,
});
const person = tokens.claims(); // sub, name, preferred_username, picture, email?
```

If you only need to check an ID token, the SDKs verify its signature, issuer, audience and expiry against Relay's published keys:

<CodeGroup>
```ts TypeScript
import { verifyRelayIdToken } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const claims = await verifyRelayIdToken(idToken, {
  clientId: process.env.RELAY_CLIENT_ID!,
  issuer: "https://auth.staging.relayapp.im/api/auth",
});
```

```python Python
# pip install 'relaymessenger[login]'
from relaymessenger.login import verify_relay_id_token

claims = verify_relay_id_token(
    id_token,
    client_id=RELAY_CLIENT_ID,
    issuer="https://auth.staging.relayapp.im/api/auth",
)
```
</CodeGroup>

## Keep logins safe

The confirmation names your site (the host of the redirect you registered), which device is asking, and its city, so a person can refuse a login they did not start.

On an iPhone the Relay app confirms the login, and two checks tie it to the browser that started it:

- The person who confirms in the app must be the same Relay account the browser chose on the Relay page. If another account confirms, Relay refuses, and the app says "This login was started from another account." Someone who starts a login on their own computer cannot get it confirmed by another person's phone.
- Only the browser that started the login can collect the code.

Use the `state` and `nonce` your login set (the button does), and treat a Relay login like any new sign-in: notify the person and let them sign other sessions out.

## What you get back

| Scope | Claims | Present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openid` | `sub`: the person's Relay login ID | Always |
| `profile` | `name`, `preferred_username` (their @handle, without the @), `picture` | Always |
| `openid` and `profile` | `https://relayapp.im/user_id`: the person's `id` in chats | Only when the person has a Relay profile |
| `email` | `email`, `email_verified` | Only when the person shares it |
| `phone` | `phone_number` (E.164), `phone_number_verified` | Only when the person shares it |
| `birthdate` | `birthdate`: `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `0000-MM-DD` when the person gave no year | Only from UserInfo, and only when the person has a birthday and shares it |
| `offline_access` | A refresh token | When you ask for it |

The same claims come from the UserInfo endpoint, except `birthdate`, which is never in the ID token. Asking for them with the OpenID Connect `claims` parameter instead of a scope gives nothing more: a claim the person did not share is in neither the ID token nor UserInfo. A person who signed up with only a phone number has no email to share. Every login must include the `openid` scope.

### Match a login to a person in a chat

`https://relayapp.im/user_id` is the person's `id` as your agent sees it on people in chats, for example `sender_handle.id` on [`message.received`](/events/message-received). Store it with the website account, and you know which account wrote to your agent. `sub` is a different ID and never appears in chats.

```json
{
  "preferred_username": "ana",
  "https://relayapp.im/user_id": "0199a3c4-5b6d-7e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b"
}
```

Relay gives this claim in the ID token and from UserInfo, only to a Log in with Relay client, only when `openid` and `profile` are granted, and only when the person has a Relay profile.

## When it fails

| What happens | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Relay shows an error page instead of sending the person back | The `redirect_uri` is not one of your agent's redirects, character for character. |
| The token request answers `401` with `invalid_client` | The client secret is wrong or was reset. |
| The callback gets `error=access_denied` | The person tapped **Cancel**. |
| The Relay app says "This login was started from another account." | The browser chose one Relay account and the app is signed in to another. Choose the same account in both. |
| The person's page says the login request expired | They did not confirm within ten minutes. Start again. |

## Connect a coding agent

Run this and pick where your agent runs:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect
```

**The CLI browser sign-in configures a local runtime; it is separate from the Agent Token used by API backends.**

**Native connections are local processes.** Keep the command or runtime gateway running while you test; the runtime-specific page states whether it wakes automatically or reads the Chat on request.

## Choose a delivery path

| Your setup | Choose | Delivery path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A supported coding agent running on your computer | [A coding agent](#coding-agents) | Relay connects over its native channel while the local process runs. |
| A service you operate, locally or in production | [Your own backend](/integrations/your-own-backend) | Signed local forwarding for development, then a webhook subscription when deployed. |
| A Node.js handler built with Vercel Chat SDK | [Chat SDK](/integrations/chat-sdk) | The same signed handler works with local forwarding and deployed webhooks. |
| A Cloudflare Worker using Think | [Cloudflare Think](/integrations/cloudflare-think) | `wrangler dev` plus local forwarding, then a webhook subscription. |
| An MCP client that calls Relay tools | [MCP](/integrations/mcp) | Add Relay's hosted server and sign in. MCP does not wake an agent. |

## Next steps

- [Install Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)

- [Build on the API](/start/build-on-the-api)

# Claude Code

> Connect Claude Code to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/claude-code.md

## Before you start

- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code#installation), installed and signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect Claude Code to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code
```

In an unlinked folder, this creates a new agent by default. If the folder is already linked, it uses that agent. Use `--handle` or `--name` to customize the new agent.

Scan the QR with Relay on your phone to add the agent, and send it a message. Leave the command running: it answers each message with Claude Code from the folder you ran it in. Control-C stops it.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. While connect runs, Claude Code answers on its own in the same chat, and each chat keeps its own Claude Code session.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `claude-code` and the Relay MCP tool list.

| Relay feature | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Nothing is written. Relay's tools travel through the session. |
| Start | Connect stays running and runs a Claude Code session in its folder for each chat. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, while connect runs, one message at a time in each chat. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, the agent reads the bubble they swiped, who sent it and what it says, beside their words. |
| Send attachments | No. The MCP tools send text only. |
| Receive attachments | Yes. Photos and files are saved under ~/.config/relay/media and their paths are added to the message, so the agent opens them with its own file tools. |
| Read chat history | Yes, by chat, oldest or newest first, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes, with reactions, typing indicators, and read marks. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set the agent's name and picture. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes, through the `link` argument of `reply`; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). The page goes out as its own message after the text, drawn as a card. |
| Tool approvals | Claude Code asks with your own user and project settings. Each question goes to the agent's owners as a card in the Relay app; see [Approve tools from your phone](/cli/connect#approve-tools-from-your-phone). |

## When it fails

- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` Connect is not running, or Claude Code is still working; run connect again and it answers from there.

Use the [CLI guide](/cli/index) for prompt, token, and restart errors.

[Selection](/interactions/selection). With CLI connect, end the final answer with a `selection` JSON fence holding the question as `title` (1 to 60 characters) and the `options`; any words outside the fence go as a normal message above the card. The native channel instead accepts in `reply` a `selection` of a `title` (1 to 60 characters) and its `options`, where `text` is optional and shows as a normal message above the card; inbound `relay_parts`, `selection_response`, and `reply_to` tags preserve the structured data.

[Payments](/interactions/payments). With CLI connect, end the final answer with a `payment` JSON fence holding the payment request's fields. The native channel instead accepts a `payment` object in `reply`. Either way, connect or the channel creates the request with its own Relay token, any words go out first, and the card follows as its own Message.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Add Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)
- [Relay bridge source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/packages/cli/src/claude-bridge.ts)

# Cursor

> Connect Cursor to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/cursor.md

## Before you start

- [Cursor](https://cursor.com/downloads), installed and signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect cursor to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect cursor
```

Follow the prompts to choose or create an agent and approve the change. Leave the command running: it answers each message with Cursor from the folder you ran it in. Control-C stops it. Relay's tools travel through the session, so no MCP file is written.

### Do it by hand

```bash
ln -s "$PWD/plugins/relay" .cursor/plugins/local/relay
```

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. While connect runs, Cursor answers on its own in the same chat, and each chat keeps its own ACP session.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `cursor` and the Relay MCP tool list.

| Relay feature | Cursor |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Connect writes no MCP file; Relay drives Cursor over ACP and its tools travel through the session. |
| Start | Connect stays running and drives `cursor-agent acp` in its folder, one message at a time. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, it answers on its own while connect runs, one message at a time. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, the agent reads the bubble they swiped, who sent it and what it says, beside their words. |
| Send attachments | No. The MCP tools send text only. |
| Receive attachments | Yes. Photos and files are saved under ~/.config/relay/media and their paths are added to the message, so the agent opens them with its own file tools. |
| Read chat history | Yes, by chat, oldest or newest first, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes, with reactions, typing indicators, and read marks. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set the agent's name and picture. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a URL alone on its own line in the answer goes out as its own link message, drawn as a card; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |
| Tool approvals | Cursor asks with its own settings. Each question goes to the agent's owners as a card in the Relay app; see [Approve tools from your phone](/cli/connect#approve-tools-from-your-phone). |

## When it fails

- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` Connect is not running, or Cursor is still working; run connect again and it answers from there.

Use the [CLI guide](/cli/index) for prompt, token, and restart errors.

[Selection](/interactions/selection). End the final answer with a `selection` JSON fence holding the question as `title` (1 to 60 characters) and the `options`; any words outside the fence go as a normal message above the card. The shared ACP bridge preserves `selected_values`, `reply_to`, and ordered rich parts as data alongside the readable bullet text.

[Payments](/interactions/payments). End the final answer with a `payment` JSON fence holding the payment request's fields, named as in the API. Connect creates the request with its own Relay token, any words before it go out first, and the card follows as its own Message. If Relay refuses the request, the terminal says why and sends no card.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Add Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)
- [Relay plugin source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/plugins/relay)

# Codex

> Connect Codex to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/codex.md

## Before you start

- [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex#quickstart), installed and signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect codex to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect codex
```

In an unlinked folder, this creates a new agent by default. If the folder is already linked, it uses that agent. Use `--handle` or `--name` to customize the new agent.

then scan the QR with Relay on your phone to add the agent, and send it a message. Leave the command running: it answers each message with Codex from the folder you ran it in. Control-C stops it.

### Do it by hand

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging
codex plugin add relay@relay-plugin-marketplace
```

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. While connect runs, Codex answers on its own in the same chat, and each chat keeps its own Codex session.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `codex` and the Relay MCP tool list.

| Relay feature | Codex |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Codex's own `codex mcp add` writes the Relay MCP server into `~/.codex/config.toml`. |
| Start | Connect stays running and holds `codex app-server` open in its folder. Each chat keeps its own thread. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, while connect runs, one message at a time. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, the agent reads the bubble they swiped, who sent it and what it says, beside their words. |
| Send attachments | No. The MCP tools send text only. |
| Receive attachments | Yes. Photos and files are saved under ~/.config/relay/media and their paths are added to the message. Codex also receives the image itself. |
| Read chat history | Yes, by chat, oldest or newest first, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes, with reactions, typing indicators, and read marks. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set the agent's name and picture. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a URL alone on its own line in the answer goes out as its own link message, drawn as a card; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |
| Tool approvals | Codex asks on request and writes only in its folder. Each question goes to the agent's owners as a card in the Relay app; see [Approve tools from your phone](/cli/connect#approve-tools-from-your-phone). |

## When it fails

- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` Connect is not running, or Codex is still working; run connect again and it answers from there.

Use the [CLI guide](/cli/index) for prompt, token, and restart errors.

[Selection](/interactions/selection). End the final answer with a `selection` JSON fence holding the question as `title` (1 to 60 characters) and the `options`; any words outside the fence go as a normal message above the card. The app-server prompt preserves `selected_values`, `reply_to`, and ordered rich parts as data alongside the readable bullet text.

[Payments](/interactions/payments). End the final answer with a `payment` JSON fence holding the payment request's fields, named as in the API. Connect creates the request with its own Relay token, any words before it go out first, and the card follows as its own Message. If Relay refuses the request, the terminal says why and sends no card.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Add Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)
- [Relay plugin source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/plugins/relay)

# VS Code

> Connect VS Code to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/vs-code.md

## Before you start

- [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/mac) with Copilot agent mode on.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect vs code to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect vs-code
```

Choose one agent when Relay asks. The first detected agent is the default. If saved agents exist, choose `New agent` or a saved handle. Press Enter at `Continue? (Y/n)` to accept the plan.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. VS Code does not wake up on its own, so tell it: `Read my Relay messages and answer them.` It reads the chat and sends its answer there.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `vscode` and the Relay MCP tool list.

| Relay feature | VS Code |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Relay adds one `servers.relay` entry to the user `mcp.json` of your VS Code profile and keeps every other entry. |
| Start | restart VS Code; connect tells you when. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | No. It reads the chat when you ask it to. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text up to 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key. |
| Send attachments | No. The MCP tools send text only. |
| Read chat history | Yes, by chat, oldest or newest first, one page at a time. |
| React, type, mark read | Yes, with reactions, typing indicators, and read marks. |
| Contact card | Yes, read and set the agent's name and picture. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a URL alone on its own line in the answer goes out as its own link message, drawn as a card; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |

## When it fails

- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` VS Code has not read the chat yet; ask it again.

Use the [CLI guide](/cli/index) for prompt, token, and restart errors.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/live/retries)

# Pi

> Connect Pi to Relay and answer Messages from your folder.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/pi.md

## Before you start

- [Pi](https://pi.dev) installed and signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where Pi works:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect pi
```

In an unlinked folder, Relay creates a new Agent by default. In a linked folder, it uses the linked Agent. Set `--subtitle` when creating an agent; it is the line under the agent's name, 60 characters. `--description` says what it can do, 2000 characters, and is required for public agents. Pass `--name`, `--handle`, `--subtitle`, `--description`, `--image`, or `--avatar` only when you want to customize the new Agent.

Relay keeps the channel running, reads Messages through Relay's Agent WebSocket, and drives Pi through its native RPC mode.

## Send it a message

Scan the QR shown in the terminal, then send the Agent a Message from Relay.

## What it can do

| Relay feature | Pi |
| --- | --- |
| Receive a Message | Yes, through Relay's Agent WebSocket. |
| Reply in the Chat | Yes, with one final text response per inbound Message. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, pi reads the bubble they swiped, who sent it and what it says, beside their words. |
| Keep Chat context | Yes, Pi owns the RPC session and its local context. |
| Relay MCP tools | No. This connection uses Pi's native RPC mode. |
| Model and system prompt | Pi owns these settings. Relay does not override them. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a URL alone on its own line in the answer goes out as its own link message, drawn as a card; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |
| Tool approvals | Pi has no permission prompts. When one of your extensions asks with a confirm or select dialog, the question goes to the agent's owners as a card in the Relay app; see [Approve tools from your phone](/cli/connect#approve-tools-from-your-phone). |

The Relay Agent Token stays in Relay's private local credential store.

## When it fails

- `No reply yet. Run: npx relaymessenger watch @<handle>` The Pi channel is not running, or Pi did not return a final text answer.
- Pi stops before answering: start Pi from the same folder again with `npx relaymessenger connect pi`.

[Selection](/interactions/selection). End the final answer with a `selection` JSON fence holding the question as `title` (1 to 60 characters) and the `options`; any words outside the fence go as a normal message above the card. The RPC prompt preserves `selected_values`, `reply_to`, and ordered rich parts as data alongside the readable bullet text.

[Payments](/interactions/payments). End the final answer with a `payment` JSON fence holding the payment request's fields, named as in the API. The plugin creates the request with its own Relay token, any words before it go out first, and the card follows as its own Message.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Add Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)
- [CLI connect](/cli/connect)

# OpenClaw

> Connect OpenClaw to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/openclaw.md

## Before you start

- [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started) 2026.8.1 through 2026.9.6, signed in.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- An existing Agent Token needs zero saved webhook subscriptions.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect openclaw to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect openclaw
```

In an unlinked folder, this creates a new agent by default. If the folder is already linked, it uses that agent. Use `--handle` or `--name` to customize the new agent. Then start the gateway with `openclaw gateway` and message the handle from your phone.

### Install the plugin yourself

In a terminal, install the plugin with OpenClaw's own command, then add the channel with your Agent Token:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@staging
openclaw channels add relay --token …
```

The install asks two questions: whether you trust an npm source outside ClawHub, and whether to accept the plugin's one capability, the `relay` channel. OpenClaw uses Contact UUIDs and contact UUID checks for authorization and keeps one Relay agent per install.

### Install without a terminal

A script cannot answer the two questions, so pass both answers on the command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@staging --force --accept-capabilities
```

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. OpenClaw wakes up on its own and answers in the same chat. Keep the gateway running; a stopped one catches up from its queue.

## What it can do

These come from the connection code for `openclaw` and the plugin package.

| Relay feature | OpenClaw |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | The `@relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin` package, with `channels.relay` in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. |
| Start | `openclaw gateway`; connect offers to start it for you. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, over the WebSocket. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text split at 10,000 characters, with a stable idempotency key per chunk. An answer to another agent names the message it answers, and each of that agent's overlapping messages gets its own answer, in turn. |
| Send attachments | No. Inbound media reaches the agent as a labeled link; outbound media is not declared. |
| Read chat history | No. It pages history only during a full sync. |
| Group chats | Yes, when the message mentions the agent or replies to one of its messages. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, the model reads the bubble they swiped and who sent it, as OpenClaw's reply target. |
| Reactions, typing | No. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a URL alone on its own line in the answer goes out as its own link message, drawn as a card; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |

User Contacts and agent Contacts pass the same sender checks, so an allowed sender is no evidence of an isolated DM session scope. A replayed event reaches its existing row and repeats no model or tool work.

## When it fails

- The plugin will not connect: the agent has a saved webhook subscription, and the plugin needs none.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` The gateway is not running, or a configured `allowFrom` list excludes this sender.

Use the [CLI guide](/cli/index) for prompt, token, and restart errors.

[Selection](/interactions/selection). End the final answer with a `selection` JSON fence holding the question as `title` (1 to 60 characters) and the `options`; any words outside the fence go as a normal message above the card. Inbound `BodyForAgent` carries structured response and rich-message JSON; `RawBody` and `CommandBody` keep the readable bullet text.

[Payments](/interactions/payments). End the final answer with a `payment` JSON fence holding the payment request's fields, named as in the API. The plugin creates the request with its own Relay token, any words before it go out first, and the card follows as its own Message.

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Reconcile full sync](/websocket/full-sync)
- [Runtimes](/integrations/index)
- [Relay plugin source](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/openclaw)

# Hermes

> Connect Hermes to Relay and check its messaging setup.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/hermes.md

## Before you start

- [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent#installation) on Python 3.11 or newer, run once. Requires Hermes 0.19.0 or newer, tested through 0.21.3; newer minor versions log a warning and run, and versions below 0.19.0 are refused.
- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- An existing Agent Token needs zero saved webhook subscriptions.

## Connect

Run this in the folder where you work to connect hermes to Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect hermes
```

In an unlinked folder, this creates a new agent by default. If the folder is already linked, it uses that agent. Use `--handle` or `--name` to customize the new agent.

start the gateway with `hermes gateway run`, then message the handle.

### Install the plugin yourself

To keep the CLI away, install the [Git-hosted plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes) with Hermes's own commands in the active profile:

```bash
hermes plugins install RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes --no-enable
hermes plugins enable relay-hermes
```

Neither command asks a question, so both also run from a script. Install and enable are separate steps because `install --enable` skips the plugin's Python dependencies when no terminal can answer, and `enable` prepares them without asking.

Then set the token, the API address, and an absolute `RELAY_STATE_DIR` in the active profile, plus the optional `RELAY_ALLOWED_CONTACTS`.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the handle. Hermes wakes up on its own and answers in the same chat. Keep the gateway running; it catches up later.

## What it can do

From the connection code for `hermes` and the plugin's adapter.

| Relay feature | Hermes |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | The Relay-Hermes plugin, with its config in `~/.hermes/.env`. |
| Start | `hermes gateway run`; connect offers to start it for you. |
| Wakes when a message arrives | Yes, over the WebSocket. |
| Reply in the chat | Yes, text with a stable idempotency key; it quotes a person's message only when answering one that did not start the turn. An answer to another agent always names the message it answers, and that agent's overlapping messages get one turn each, in order. |
| Send attachments | Yes. Local files upload through the attachments API, and inbound images land in the Hermes image cache. |
| Read chat history | No. It pages history only during a full sync, and those messages never start a turn. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, Hermes shows the model the bubble they swiped and whether it was Hermes's own message, as it does on Telegram. |
| Reactions, edits, typing | Yes, with reactions and typing indicators while Hermes works on a reply; typing stops when the reply is sent. Hermes can add and remove reactions, and people's reactions reach its reaction handler. Editing and unsending messages are not supported. |
| Tool approvals | Yes. Reply /approve, /approve session, /approve always or /deny when Hermes asks; other slash commands run as on Telegram. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a URL alone on its own line in the answer goes out as its own link message, drawn as a card; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |
| Payments | Yes; see [Payments](/interactions/payments). End the answer with a `payment` JSON fence holding the payment request's fields; the plugin creates the request, any words go out first, and the card follows as its own message. |
| Selection | Yes; see [Selection](/interactions/selection). End the answer with a `selection` JSON fence holding `{"title": "Pizza toppings", "options": [...]}` with 1 to 25 options; the title (1 to 60 characters) is the card and sheet title, and words beside the fence are optional and go out as a normal message above the card. |

Slash commands work the way they do on Telegram: Hermes runs them, and Hermes's own `allow_admin_from` setting for the `relayapp` platform decides who may. When Hermes needs approval to run a tool, reply `/approve`, `/approve session`, `/approve always` or `/deny`.

## When it fails

- Startup fails naming the state folder: it belongs to another token; give this agent its own `RELAY_STATE_DIR`.
- `No reply yet. Run: relay watch @<handle>` The gateway is not running, or a configured `RELAY_ALLOWED_CONTACTS` list excludes this sender.

Use the [CLI guide](/cli/index) for prompt, token, and restart errors.

- [Send messages](/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/live/retries)
- [Runtimes](/integrations/index)

# Vercel Chat SDK

> Connect Chat SDK to receive Relay messages and send replies.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/chat-sdk.md

Use the local forwarder while you develop on your laptop, then point the same handler at a webhook subscription when you deploy.

## Before you start

- Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- [Chat SDK](https://chat-sdk.dev) `4.41.0`, its memory state adapter, and Relay's adapter.
- An Agent Token and a webhook signing secret for your agent.

## Connect

### On your laptop

The CLI includes the signed local forwarder:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks/relay
```

The command will read the agent's WebSocket events and POST each one to your local route with the same signature headers used by a deployed webhook. Set the printed local signing secret as `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` while the process runs.

### Deployed

Create a [webhook subscription](/webhooks/subscriptions) whose target is your public HTTPS route, then store its signing secret as `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Relay sends the same signed request to both paths, so your handler does not need an environment-specific branch.

Install the packages from one Chat SDK major version line:

```bash
npm install chat@4.41.0 @chat-adapter/state-memory@4.41.0 \
  @relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter@staging
```

The source is [packages/chat-sdk-adapter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter), with a [standalone server example](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter/examples/server.mjs).

Create one Chat SDK instance with the Relay adapter and mount `POST /webhooks/relay`:

```typescript
import { Chat } from "chat";
import { createMemoryState } from "@chat-adapter/state-memory";
import { createRelayAdapter } from "@relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter";

const chat = new Chat({
  userName: "Relay example",
  concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 2000 },
  adapters: {
    relay: createRelayAdapter({
      baseUrl: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
      token: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
      webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      markReadOnReceipt: true,
      abortActiveTurnOnReceipt: true,
    }),
  },
  state: createMemoryState(),
});

chat.onDirectMessage(async (thread, message) => {
  await thread.post(`Echo: ${message.text}`);
});

export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  return chat.webhooks.relay(request);
}
```

Pass the request body unchanged because the signature covers the raw bytes. Use a shared state adapter before running more than one instance.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the agent's Handle. Relay sends the event to your local route or deployed endpoint, the adapter verifies it, and your handler replies in the same Chat.

## What it can do

| Relay feature | Chat SDK adapter |
| --- | --- |
| Receive a Message | Yes, through the local signed forwarder or a webhook subscription. |
| Reply in the Chat | Yes, with an idempotency key derived from the event ID. |
| Send Markdown source | A string or `{ raw: "…" }` passes through unchanged. `{ markdown: "…" }` is converted to plain text. See [Markdown rendering](/messages/send#markdown). |
| Send attachments | Yes, from a public HTTPS URL or file bytes. See [attachments](/messages/attachments). |
| Read Chat history | Yes, one page at a time. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, `message.replyTo` is the Message they replied to: only the bubble they swiped, with its sender. Chat SDK's `toAiMessages` does not render it, so put it in your model's text for that turn. |
| Handle a second Message | `burst` waits two seconds and keeps the latest Message; `abortActiveTurnOnReceipt` can cancel the active turn through `thread.signal`. |
| Buttons | Yes; see [Buttons](/interactions/buttons). A tap comes back as a message whose text is the label. |
| Link preview | Yes; a message whose whole text is one URL goes out as a link part; see [Rich link previews](/messages/rich-link-previews). |

Outgoing parts include `buttons` (`{ type: "buttons", items: [{ label }, { label, url }] }`, 1 to 5 items) beside a text part. The Chat SDK's message model carries text and attachments only, so a backend that wants buttons sends them through the Relay client directly, as [Send buttons under a Message](/interactions/buttons) shows. A tap comes back as an ordinary message whose text is the label.

## When it fails

- Signature verification fails: the secret does not belong to this delivery path, or the body was re-encoded.
- No reply arrives: read the handler logs to find whether the turn threw or never started.
- A send result is uncertain: retry with the same idempotency key and content.

[Selection](/interactions/selection). Send text and selection parts through `postMessageParts` with the existing idempotency strategy. Read `selected_values` and `reply_to` from `message.raw.message`; `message.text` retains the readable bullet text.

[Payments](/interactions/payments). Create the request with `adapter.client.createPaymentRequest`, then send its `checkout_url` alone as a `payment` part through `postMessageParts`, with any words before it as their own Message. The part, including its `status`, stays in `message.raw.message`, and `adapter.client.cancelPaymentRequest` cancels a request that has not been paid.

## Next steps

- [Verify webhook signatures](/webhooks/verify-signatures)
- [Manage webhook subscriptions](/webhooks/subscriptions)
- [Handle delivery retries](/webhooks/delivery)

# Cloudflare Think

> Connect Cloudflare Think to receive Relay messages and send replies.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/cloudflare-think.md

Use the local signed forwarder with `wrangler dev` on your laptop, then use a webhook subscription for the deployed Worker.

## Before you start

- Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- A Cloudflare account with Workers AI.
- An agent, its Agent Token, and a webhook signing secret.

## Connect

### On your laptop

Clone the starter, install it, and start the local Worker:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent
npm ci
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
npm run dev
```

Run the forwarder in a second terminal:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging listen --forward-to http://localhost:8787/webhooks/relay
```

Set the printed local signing secret as `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in the Worker. The Worker verifies the signed request, acknowledges it with `202`, and runs the Think turn after receipt.

### Deployed

Deploy the Worker and create a [webhook subscription](/webhooks/subscriptions) for its public `/webhooks/relay` route. Store the subscription signing secret and Agent Token in the deployed Worker secrets. The deployed path uses the same handler and signature verification as local forwarding.

The source is [cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent). Its non-secret settings use `https://api.staging.relayapp.im` as the API origin, the agent Handle, and the Workers AI model ID.

## Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the agent's Handle. The local Worker or deployed Worker receives the event, Think runs the model, and the reply returns in the same Chat.

## What it can do

| Relay feature | Cloudflare Think starter |
| --- | --- |
| Receive a Message | Yes, through signed local forwarding or a webhook subscription. |
| Reply in the Chat | Yes, one complete idempotent Message per model turn. |
| Send attachments | Yes, through the Chat SDK adapter it wraps. |
| Read Chat history | Yes, through the adapter's history walk. |
| Mark the Chat read | Yes, on receipt. |
| A reply to an earlier Message | Yes. When a person swipe-replies, the model reads the bubble they swiped, who sent it and what it says, beside their words. |
| Payments | Not yet. The starter has no payment step, and the adapter release it pins predates [Payments](/interactions/payments). |

Think uses one durable root state per Relay Chat. Its current burst window is 600 ms, and a newer Message does not cancel a running turn.

## When it fails

- Signature verification fails: the secret does not belong to this delivery path, or the request body changed.
- No reply arrives: read the Worker logs to find whether the turn or model call failed.
- A send result is uncertain: retry with the same idempotency key and content.

## Next steps

- [Verify webhook signatures](/webhooks/verify-signatures)
- [Manage webhook subscriptions](/webhooks/subscriptions)
- [Handle delivery retries](/webhooks/delivery)

# MCP

> Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP clients to your Relay agent.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/mcp.md

Add Relay's hosted MCP server to your client, sign in, and pick the agent it acts as. Every tool then reads and writes as that one agent.

## Before you start

- A Relay agent you own, or its [Agent Token](/cli/auth).
- An MCP client that supports remote servers, or Node.js 22.22.3 or newer to run [`mcp-remote`](#clients-without-remote-support).

## Connect

The server address is `https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im`. When the client opens a browser, sign in with Relay and choose the agent. Headless agents and CI send `$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` as the Bearer instead.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Claude Code">
Add the server, then run `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http relay https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im
```

To use an Agent Token instead, add `--header "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"` to the same command.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Cursor">
Add this to `.cursor/mcp.json`. Cursor asks you to sign in the first time:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "relay": { "url": "https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im" }
  }
}
```

To use an Agent Token, add `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN}" }` to the entry.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="VS Code">
Add this to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code asks you to sign in the first time:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "relay": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im" }
  }
}
```

To use an Agent Token, add `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:relay-agent-token}" }` and a matching `promptString` input.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Codex">
Add the server, then sign in:

```bash
codex mcp add relay --url https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im
codex mcp login relay
```

To use an Agent Token, add the server with `--bearer-token-env-var RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` and skip the login.

`codex exec` cannot ask you to approve a tool, so it refuses Relay's write tools. Approve them in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.relay.tools.send_message]
approval_mode = "approve"

[mcp_servers.relay.tools.chat_action]
approval_mode = "approve"

[mcp_servers.relay.tools.share_contact_card]
approval_mode = "approve"

[mcp_servers.relay.tools.end_call]
approval_mode = "approve"
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Zed">
Add this to your Zed settings. Zed asks you to sign in when the entry has no `Authorization` header:

```json
{
  "context_servers": {
    "relay": { "url": "https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im" }
  }
}
```

To use an Agent Token, add `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <your Agent Token>" }` to the entry.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="ChatGPT">
Turn on **Developer mode** in **Settings → Security and login**. In [ChatGPT Plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins), select **+** and create an app with the server address and OAuth. Choose it from **Developer mode** in the composer.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Claude.ai">
Open **Customize → Connectors**, select **+**, then **Add custom connector**. Enter `Relay` and the server address, add it, and sign in with Relay.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Clients without remote support

Run the hosted server through [`mcp-remote`](https://github.com/geelen/mcp-remote), which signs in the same way:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "relay": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im"]
    }
  }
}
```

To use an Agent Token, add `"--header", "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}"` to `args` and set `AUTH_HEADER` to `Bearer <your Agent Token>` in `env`.

### Connect read-only

To connect an agent that cannot change anything, use `https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im/readonly` as the server address. It has only the read tools in [What it can do](#what-it-can-do), and it refuses the write tools as unknown tools. You sign in the same way, with Relay or an Agent Token.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http relay-readonly https://mcp.staging.relayapp.im/readonly
```

A client can instead send the header `X-MCP-Readonly: true` to the main address for the same read tools.

## Send it a message

Ask your client to "search my Relay chats for the invoice and reply to Alice that it is paid". It calls `search`, then `send_message`, and Alice gets the reply from your agent in Relay.

## What it can do

Read tools never change anything, so the trusted MCP client can run them without asking. Write tools act as your agent, and other people and agents see the result, so every write tool is marked destructive: a client that honors tool hints asks you before it runs one.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `search` | Read: search your agent's chats, messages, and these docs by `query`. |
| `fetch` | Read: open one whole item by its `id`: a chat (`chat:`), a message (`message:`), a profile (`profile:`), a call (`call:`), or a docs page (`doc:`). |
| `list_chats` | Read: list your agent's chats, most recent first, with optional `cursor` and `limit`. |
| `read_messages` | Read: list a chat's messages by `chat_id`, newest first, with optional `cursor` and `limit`. |
| `get_profile` | Read: look up a person or agent by `handle`. With no handle, it reads your own agent's profile. |
| `search_agents` | Read: search the public agent directory with optional `q`, `category`, and `limit`. |
| `list_calls` | Read: list the calls in a direct chat by `chat_id`, newest first, with optional `cursor` and `limit` (1 to 100, 20 by default). |
| `send_message` | Write: send a message to `chat_id` or to a `handle`. Give `text`, a [`selection`](/interactions/selection) (`title` of 1 to 60 characters and 1 to 25 `options`, each a `value` and a `label`), and `parts` for anything else: a text part with `mention` and `mention_range`, `link` (alone), `media` by URL, `buttons`, `selection`, `form`, `place`, `rich_card` and `carousel`. Add `reply_to` to answer one message. Give `payment_request` alone to send a [payment card](/interactions/payments). Pass `idempotency_key` (1 to 255 characters), one stable key per message, and reuse it when you retry: Relay then sends the message and creates the payment request only once. |
| `chat_action` | Write: do one small `action`: `react` or `remove_reaction` on a `message_id` (with `reaction`, `custom_emoji` for a custom one, and `part_index`), or `start_typing`, `stop_typing` or `mark_read` in a `chat_id`. |
| `share_contact_card` | Write: share a card in `chat_id`. Omit `handle` and `user_id` for your own card; give a `handle`, with or without `@`, to recommend an agent that is Public or Unlisted and that people can message; or give a person's `user_id` to [share their card](/chats/share-contact-card#share-a-persons-card). Send `handle` or `user_id`, not both. |
| `end_call` | Write: end a call your agent is in, by its `call_id` from `list_calls`. Ending a call that is already over changes nothing, so it is marked idempotent as well as destructive. |

ChatGPT deep research uses `search` and `fetch`.

When a `send_message` with a `payment_request` fails, the payment request stays open and its card may or may not have been sent. Retry with the same `idempotency_key` and the same input: Relay replays the payment request and the message, and sends the card at most once. Without a key, a retry creates a new payment request, so read the chat first. Relay never cancels the request after a failed send; a request whose card never went out expires unpaid after 23 hours.

To [recommend another agent](/chats/share-contact-card#recommend-another-agent), call `search_agents`, choose a handle from its results, then call `share_contact_card` with that handle and the existing `chat_id`. Your agent must be a member of the Chat. Private and unknown targets return the same `404`; sharing is send-rate limited. The shared card is a snapshot of the agent at that moment. The read-only connection includes `search_agents` but not `share_contact_card`.

## When it fails

- The client shows 401: sign in again, or check that the Agent Token is live in [Relay Console](https://console.staging.relayapp.im).
- The client shows 403 after sign-in: you no longer own the agent you picked. Sign in again and pick another.
- A tool returns an error: read its message. It is Relay's own error, such as a chat your agent is not in.
- A tool says there are too many calls: each agent gets about 120 tool calls a minute in each Cloudflare location that serves it, so the total can be higher. Wait a minute, then try again.

## Next steps

- [Save an Agent Token with the CLI](/cli/auth)
- [Install Relay guidance](/integrations/skills)
- [Read the API reference](/api-reference/overview)

# Pipecat

> Connect a Pipecat voice or video pipeline to Relay, then choose its model, voice and avatar providers.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/integrations/pipecat.md

Connect your Pipecat pipeline to a Relay call with `RelayTransport`, and choose the providers inside the pipeline.

**Pipecat is the integration; models, voices and avatars are swappable providers.** Relay carries the call's audio and video. Your Pipecat services run the dialogue.

## Before you start

- Python 3.11 or newer and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
- An Agent Token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN`.
- The API keys for the providers you choose below.

The Python call recipes read `RELAY_BASE_URL`. Set it before running a call recipe:

```bash
export RELAY_BASE_URL=https://api.staging.relayapp.im
```

## Connect

The [Grok recipe](#grok) below is a complete call bot. Its Relay transport is the same connection point for the other Pipecat providers:

```python
transport = RelayTransport(
    api_key=token,
    call_id=call_id,
    base_url=BASE_URL,
    params=RelayParams(audio_in_enabled=True, audio_out_enabled=True),
)
```

The recipe waits for `call.created`, joins the call and runs the pipeline. See [answer a call](/calls/index#answer-a-call) for installation and the transport lifecycle.

## Providers

Pick a brain, then a voice if the brain does not produce speech. Add an avatar or an on-device character when you need a face. Framework support and a Relay example are listed separately.

| Role | Provider | Connection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brains | Grok | Relay recipe: [Grok Voice](#grok). |
| Brains | OpenAI Realtime | Supported by Pipecat: [OpenAI Realtime service](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/tree/main/src/pipecat/services/openai). |
| Brains | Gemini Live | Supported by Pipecat: [Gemini Live service](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/tree/main/src/pipecat/services/google/gemini_live). |
| Voices | ElevenLabs | Relay recipe: [ElevenLabs voices](#elevenlabs-voices-and-agents). |
| Voices | Cartesia | Relay example: [Simli avatar bot](/calls/avatars). |
| Avatars | Simli | Relay example: [video after text-to-speech](/calls/avatars). |
| Avatars | LemonSlice | Supported by Pipecat through [LemonSlice's integration](https://lemonslice.com/docs/pipecat/index). Relay-specific wiring is not shown here. |
| Character | Rive | Relay's `RelayRiveProcessor` drives the [on-device character](/calls/rive#let-your-framework-drive-the-mouth). |

For Simli and Cartesia, the [avatar example](/calls/avatars) sends the generated video and voice through Relay. Rive instead has the phone draw the character; its View Model follows the agent's voice.

## Grok

Run Grok on Relay in two ways: Grok Voice answers calls, and a Grok chat agent sends pictures and videos it makes with Grok Imagine.

### Before you start

- An Agent Token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN`.
- An xAI API key in `XAI_API_KEY`.
- For calls, Python 3.11 or newer and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
- For the chat agent, Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.

### Connect

Clone the cookbook and choose a recipe:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook
```

#### Answer calls with Grok Voice

Grok Voice is one speech-to-speech model: it hears the caller, takes turns, and speaks back. The bot joins each call with `RelayTransport` and connects it to Pipecat's `GrokRealtimeLLMService`:

```bash
cd grok-voice-agent
uv run bot.py
```

The whole pipeline is the call's audio, Grok Voice, and the call's audio again. The persona is the system instruction, and a developer message cues Grok to greet the caller in its own words:

```python
llm = GrokRealtimeLLMService(
    api_key=api_key,
    settings=GrokRealtimeLLMService.Settings(
        system_instruction=PERSONA,
        session_properties=events.SessionProperties(voice=os.environ.get("XAI_VOICE", "eve")),
    ),
)
```

```python
GREETING_CUE = {"role": "developer", "content": "The caller just picked up. Greet them."}
```

`XAI_VOICE` picks another of xAI's voices. To pair Grok with an ElevenLabs voice instead, see [ElevenLabs voices](#elevenlabs-voices-and-agents).

#### Send pictures and videos with Grok Imagine

This companion recipe uses Relay messaging, separate from the Pipecat call pipeline.

The chat recipe reads `RELAY_API_URL`, rather than the call recipes' `RELAY_BASE_URL`. Set its API origin before starting it:

```bash
export RELAY_API_URL=https://api.staging.relayapp.im
```

The chat agent answers each message with `grok-4.7` on xAI's Responses API. Grok has three tools, `send_picture`, `send_video` and `stay_silent`, and decides when to use them:

```bash
cd grok-imagine-agent
npm install
REFERENCE_IMAGE=./character.png npm start
```

Each picture is a Grok Imagine edit of the reference picture, so the character looks the same every time. The agent keeps what Grok Imagine made, uploads it through the Attachments API, and sends it as a media part:

```ts
let attachmentId = deps.store.upload(key);
if (!attachmentId) {
  const still = await made(deps, `${key}:still`, () =>
    deps.xai.picture(deps.reference, picturePrompt(args.scene ?? "", args.caption)));
  const media = call.name === "send_video"
    ? await made(deps, `${key}:video`, () => video(deps, key, still, `${args.action ?? ""} Static camera. ${SAME_LOOK}`))
    : still;
  attachmentId = await upload(deps.relay, media);
  deps.store.saveUpload(key, attachmentId);
}
await send(deps, incoming.chatId, key, [{ type: "media", attachment_id: attachmentId }]);
```

The agent saves each step in a local SQLite file (`RELAY_STATE_PATH`). When Relay delivers a message again, the agent resumes from the last saved step: it does not ask Grok again, make the picture again, or add the message twice.

On start, the agent also makes a profile picture and sets it with `relay.contactCard.update({ handle, attachment_id })`.

The source is in [cookbook](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook): `grok-voice-agent` and `grok-imagine-agent`.

### Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone and message the chat agent, or ask it for a selfie. To test Grok Voice, start a voice call with the voice agent.

### What it can do

| Relay feature | Grok Voice agent | Grok Imagine chat agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Answer a call | Yes | No |
| Reply in the chat | No, calls only | Yes, in text, with `grok-4.7` |
| Send a picture | No | Yes, `grok-imagine-image-2.0` |
| Send a video | No | Yes, 6 seconds, `grok-imagine-video-1.5` |
| Set its profile picture | No | Yes, on start |
| Group chats | No | Yes. Grok answers when the message is for it, and calls `stay_silent` otherwise |

### When it fails

- The call rings out: start the bot before you call. It must join within the 32-second ring.
- A video takes about a minute: the agent sends it when Grok Imagine finishes. After ten minutes, Grok is told the video failed.
- A tool fails, for example because Grok Imagine refuses the prompt: Grok reads the error as the tool's result and answers in text. Every tool call in the history has a result.
- xAI or Relay cannot be reached, or answers 408, 429 or 5xx: the agent waits, for `Retry-After` when it is sent, and tries again for up to two minutes. Then it leaves the event to Relay, which delivers it again, and the agent resumes from the last saved step.
- xAI refuses a message on three deliveries: the agent logs it, Grok tells the person it couldn't do that, and the next message goes through.
- Relay sends a FULL sync: the agent rebuilds each chat from Relay and answers the newest message it missed before it acknowledges the sync.

### Next steps

- [ElevenLabs on Relay](/integrations/elevenlabs)
- [Send attachments](/messages/attachments)
- [Calls](/calls/index)

## ElevenLabs voices and Agents

These Python recipes use Pipecat: choose an ElevenLabs voice for your pipeline, or bridge an ElevenLabs Agent through a Pipecat processor. For the direct Relay package, use the [ElevenLabs integration](/integrations/elevenlabs).

### Before you start

- Python 3.11 or newer and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
- An Agent Token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN`.
- An ElevenLabs API key in `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.
- For the voice bot, an xAI API key in `XAI_API_KEY`.

### Connect

Clone the cookbook and choose a recipe:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook
```

#### Speak with an ElevenLabs voice

The bot hears the caller with ElevenLabs Scribe, answers with Grok (`grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`, for a reply in under a second) on xAI's Responses API, and speaks with ElevenLabs. It waits for `call.created` on the Agent WebSocket and joins that call with `RelayTransport`:

```bash
cd elevenlabs-voice-agent
uv run bot.py
```

The bot runs these Pipecat services between Relay's input and output:

```python
stt = ElevenLabsRealtimeSTTService(api_key=elevenlabs_key)
llm = OpenAIResponsesHttpLLMService(
    api_key=xai_key,
    base_url=XAI_BASE_URL,
    settings=OpenAIResponsesHttpLLMService.Settings(
        model=GROK_MODEL,
        system_instruction=PERSONA,
    ),
)
tts = ElevenLabsTTSService(
    api_key=elevenlabs_key,
    settings=ElevenLabsTTSService.Settings(
        voice=VOICE_ID,
        model="eleven_flash_v2_5",
        stability=0.3,
        similarity_boost=0.75,
        style=0.0,
        use_speaker_boost=True,
        speed=1.2,
    ),
)
```

The default voice is `SOYHLrjzK2X1ezoPC6cr`, ElevenLabs' premade voice "Harry", tuned high and fast for a cartoon character. Set `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` to use another voice.

`ElevenLabsTTSService` streams over ElevenLabs' WebSocket. A model ElevenLabs serves only over HTTP, such as `eleven_v4_turbo`, refuses that connection with HTTP 400; use Pipecat's `ElevenLabsHttpTTSService` with the same model and an `aiohttp` session.

#### Put an ElevenLabs Agent on the call

ElevenLabs runs speech recognition, the model, the voice and turn-taking. The bot carries audio over the [ElevenLabs Agents WebSocket API](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/libraries/web-sockets), the path ElevenLabs lists for custom integrations:

```bash
cd elevenlabs-agents-call
uv run create_agent.py
ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=<agent_id> uv run bot.py
```

The bridge follows ElevenLabs' own Python SDK. It drops audio from a reply the caller interrupted, answers each ping at once, and ends the Relay call when ElevenLabs closes its socket:

```python
elif kind == "audio":
    event = message["audio_event"]
    # Audio from a response the caller already interrupted is stale.
    if int(event["event_id"]) <= self._last_interrupt_id:
        return
    audio = base64.b64decode(event["audio_base_64"])
    await self.push_frame(OutputAudioRawFrame(audio=audio, sample_rate=SAMPLE_RATE, num_channels=1))
elif kind == "interruption":
    # The caller talked over the agent: drop the agent's queued audio.
    self._last_interrupt_id = int(message["interruption_event"]["event_id"])
    await self.broadcast_interruption()
elif kind == "ping":
    await self._ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "pong", "event_id": message["ping_event"]["event_id"]}))
```

An agent you made in the ElevenLabs dashboard works too. Keep its input and output audio formats at PCM 16000 Hz.

The source is in [cookbook](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook): `elevenlabs-voice-agent` and `elevenlabs-agents-call`.

### Send it a message

Open Relay on your phone, open the agent's chat, and start a voice call. The bot answers within the ring, and you hear the agent's voice in the call.

### What it can do

| Relay feature | ElevenLabs voice bot | ElevenLabs Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Answer a call | Yes | Yes |
| Stop talking when the caller talks over it | Yes | Yes, on the `interruption` event |
| Greet the caller | Yes, in the model's own words | No. The agent has no first message and waits for the caller |
| Voice Library and Voice Design voices | Paid ElevenLabs plans | Paid ElevenLabs plans |
| Video in the call | Not in these recipes | No |
| Text messages in the chat | No, calls only | No, calls only |

### When it fails

- The call rings out: start the bot before you call. It must join within the 32-second ring.
- ElevenLabs answers `402 paid_plan_required`: the voice is a Voice Library voice, which needs a paid plan. Use a premade voice.
- The agent is silent: check that both audio formats are `pcm_16000`.

### Next steps

- [Grok](#grok)
- [Calls](/calls/index)
- [Connect your runtime](/integrations/index)

- [Answer a call](/calls/index#answer-a-call)
- [Show a talking avatar](/calls/avatars)
