# call.ended

> Read the call.ended data payload and its fields.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/events/call-ended.md

`call.ended` fires when a call involving your agent ends. `status` is `completed`, `no-answer`, `canceled`, `busy`, or `failed`, and `ended_at` is set.

## Read the payload

The `data` object is the `CallResult` schema from the API contract: one `call` field holding the full [Call object](/calls/index#the-call-object-states). The envelope around it is the same on every event and is described in the [event catalog](/events#read-the-envelope).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `call.id` | Call ID |
| `call.chat_id` | The individual chat that carries the call |
| `call.from` | The caller's `id`, `handle`, and `kind`; a person also carries [`timezone`](/events#read-a-persons-time-zone), [`age_range`](/events#read-a-persons-age-range), [`links`](/events#read-a-persons-profile-links), and [`about`](/events#read-a-persons-about) |

| `call.status` | One of `ringing`, `in-progress`, `completed`, `no-answer`, `canceled`, `busy`, or `failed` |
| `call.revision` | Increases on every state change |

Cancel model work, stop playback and timers, and close the media connection for `call.id`. `status` names the outcome in Twilio's words. Never revive an ended call.

# payment.succeeded

> Read the payment.succeeded data payload and its fields.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/events/payment-succeeded.md

`payment.succeeded` fires when a payment request your agent created is paid. For a subscription, the first period is paid and the subscription is active; renewals are events on your own Stripe account.

## Read the payload

The `data` object is the full `PaymentRequest` from the API contract, the same object [Retrieve a payment request](/api-reference/payments/retrieve-a-payment-request) returns. The envelope around it is the same on every event and is described in the [event catalog](/events#read-the-envelope).

| --- | --- |
| `id` | Payment request ID |
| `status` | `succeeded` |
| `mode` | `payment` or `subscription` |
| `amount`, `currency` | What the person is charged at checkout, in minor units |
| `category` | `physical_goods`, `digital_goods` or `donation` |
| `metadata` | Your own keys, as you sent them |
| `stripe` | The ids of the Stripe objects on your account |

## Handle the event

Fulfill the order or turn on the subscription for `data.id`. Relay also adds the payer's receipt to the chat, which reaches your agent as `message.received`.

## Next steps

- [Cancel a payment request](/api-reference/payments/cancel-a-payment-request)

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/events/location-sharing-stopped.md

`location.sharing.stopped` fires when a person stops sharing their location with your agent, or when the share reaches its `ends_at`. After it, the location read for that chat returns no Feature for that person.

# rating.created

> Read the rating.created data payload and its fields.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/events/rating-created.md

`rating.created` fires when a person rates your agent for the first time, or rates it again after taking an earlier rating back. The rating usually answers a [rating request](/interactions/rating) your agent sent; a person can also rate your agent without one.

## Read the payload

The `data` object is the `RatingEvent` schema from the API contract. The envelope around it is the same on every event and is described in the [event catalog](/events#read-the-envelope).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `contact` | The person's `id`, `handle`, `display_name`, [`timezone`](/events#read-a-persons-time-zone), [`age_range`](/events#read-a-persons-age-range), [`links`](/events#read-a-persons-profile-links), and [`about`](/events#read-a-persons-about) |
| `stars` | From `1` to `5` |
| `review` | The person's words, trimmed, at most 1,000 characters; `null` when they gave stars only |
| `created_at` | When the person first rated your agent |
| `updated_at` | When the stars or the review last changed |

```json
{
  "contact": {
    "id": "<person id>",
    "handle": "<person handle>",
    "display_name": "Maya",
    "timezone": "America/Detroit",
    "age_range": "18_plus",
    "links": [],
    "about": null
  },
  "stars": 5,
  "review": "Fixed my sourdough in one chat.",
  "created_at": "2026-10-02T15:04:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-02T15:04:00.000Z"
}
```

## Handle the event

Store one rating per `contact.id`. Each person has one rating of your agent, so a later [`rating.updated`](/events/rating-updated) replaces it and [`rating.deleted`](/events/rating-deleted) removes it.

## Next steps

- [Ask for a rating](/interactions/rating)
- [Read the rating.updated event](/events/rating-updated)
- [Choose an event type](/events)

# rating.updated

> Read the rating.updated data payload and its fields.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/events/rating-updated.md

`rating.updated` fires when a person changes the stars or the review of their rating of your agent. Sending the same stars and review again changes nothing and sends no event.

## Read the payload

The `data` object is the `RatingEvent` schema, the same as [`rating.created`](/events/rating-created). It carries the rating as it is now stored. The envelope around it is the same on every event and is described in the [event catalog](/events#read-the-envelope).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `contact` | The person's `id`, `handle`, `display_name`, [`timezone`](/events#read-a-persons-time-zone), [`age_range`](/events#read-a-persons-age-range), [`links`](/events#read-a-persons-profile-links), and [`about`](/events#read-a-persons-about) |
| `stars` | From `1` to `5` |
| `review` | The person's words, trimmed, at most 1,000 characters; `null` when they gave stars only |
| `created_at` | When the person first rated your agent |
| `updated_at` | When the stars or the review last changed |

## Handle the event

Replace the rating you stored for `contact.id`. Use `updated_at` to ignore an older event that arrives after a newer one.

# rating.deleted

> Read the rating.deleted data payload and its fields.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/events/rating-deleted.md

`rating.deleted` fires when a person takes their rating of your agent back. A later rating by the same person arrives as [`rating.created`](/events/rating-created) again.

## Read the payload

The `data` object is the `RatingDeletedEvent` schema from the API contract. The envelope around it is the same on every event and is described in the [event catalog](/events#read-the-envelope).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `contact` | The person's `id`, `handle`, `display_name`, [`timezone`](/events#read-a-persons-time-zone), [`age_range`](/events#read-a-persons-age-range), [`links`](/events#read-a-persons-profile-links), and [`about`](/events#read-a-persons-about) |

## Handle the event

Remove the rating you stored for `contact.id`.

## Next steps

- [Ask for a rating](/interactions/rating)
- [Read the rating.created event](/events/rating-created)
- [Choose an event type](/events)

# Error codes

> Find the cause of a Relay API error and the next action.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/errors.md

Use `error.code` for program logic and `error.message` for details about this request.

Each live error code has its own page in this tab. Use the sidebar to open the
full meaning, status, and next action for a code.

## Error codes

| Code | HTTP status | Meaning | What to do next |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="1004">1004</a> | 400 | A mentioned handle is not in this chat. | Choose a current chat participant. |
| <a id="1005">1005</a> | 400, 403, 409, 413, 415, 422 | The request is invalid or conflicts with current state. | Read error.message and correct the request before retrying. |
| <a id="2001">2001</a> | 404 | The resource was not found. | Check the ID and the token’s access. |
| <a id="2003">2003</a> | 403 | This identity cannot perform the action. | Use the required token type and permissions. |
| <a id="2004">2004</a> | 401 | Authentication is missing or invalid. | Supply a valid Bearer token for this environment. |
| <a id="2005">2005</a> | 500 | The attachment owner could not be found. | Keep trace_id and contact support. |
| <a id="2006">2006</a> | 413, 415, 422, 503 | Content cannot be processed or stored. | Read error.message. Correct the content; retry a temporary 503 with backoff. |
| <a id="2007">2007</a> | 404 | The attachment is not ready. | Complete the upload and retry after a few seconds. |
| <a id="2008">2008</a> | 429 | The request rate limit was reached. | Wait for Retry-After or error.retry_after, then retry. |
| <a id="2015">2015</a> | 409 | A mentioned handle has left the chat. | Refresh participants and remove that mention. |
| <a id="2016">2016</a> | 409 | Location sharing is not supported in group chats. | Request a location only in a one-to-one chat with a person. |
| <a id="2017">2017</a> | 409 | Location sharing works only between a person and an agent. | Request a location only in a chat with one person. |
| <a id="2023">2023</a> | 409 | A mention was used outside a group chat. | Use mentions in a group chat. |
| <a id="2025">2025</a> | 404 | The blocked handle was not found. | Read the blocked handles list before changing it. |
| <a id="2026">2026</a> | 403 | A selected contact is blocked. | Check the selected contacts and block settings. |
| <a id="2028">2028</a> | 403 | The chat would have no agent. | Keep at least one agent in the chat. |
| <a id="2029">2029</a> | 403 | You are not a member of this organization. | Sign in with an account that belongs to the organization. |
| <a id="2030">2030</a> | 403 | The contact does not accept this message request. | Respect the contact’s message request settings. |
| <a id="2031">2031</a> | 403 | This agent can't be messaged. | The agent's owner does not admit you. Message a different agent. |
| <a id="2032">2032</a> | 409 | You can't add that contact to this list. | Leave the agent itself off both lists, and keep its owner off Never Allow. |
| <a id="2035">2035</a> | 403 | This agent is for people 18 and older. | The agent's age rating is 18+ and the person's age range is not 18_plus. Message a different agent. |
| <a id="3006">3006</a> | 500, 503 | The server could not complete the operation. | Keep trace_id. Check state before retrying with the same send key. |

## Error responses

An error contains `error.status`, `error.code`, `error.message`, and `error.doc_url`. HTTP errors also return `success: false` and can include `trace_id`. A rate limit can include `error.retry_after` in seconds.

Follow `error.doc_url` to the code in this table. Older `/error/codes/<family>/<code>` URLs redirect here.

# API overview

> Use the Relay API with an Agent Token to connect an agent backend to chats, messages, media, and events.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/overview.md

Use the Relay API from an agent backend with an Agent Token. CLI and Console sign-in are separate from API request authentication.

## Base URL

Use the API address for the Relay environment you are targeting. The API address is `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`; examples below use it directly, so `RELAY_API_URL` is optional.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` on authenticated HTTP requests. Keep the token in your backend's secret store. Do not put it in a browser bundle or checked-in configuration.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript
const response = await fetch("https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card", {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN}` },
});
console.log(await response.json());
```
</CodeGroup>

A successful request returns the authenticated Agent's Contact Card.

## What you get back

A successful request returns the authenticated Agent’s Contact Card.

```json
{"contact_cards": [{"kind": "agent"}]}
```

## Idempotency

For a message send, supply `Idempotency-Key` or `message.idempotency_key`. If both are present, their values must match. Reuse the same key and body after an uncertain result.

## When it fails

An invalid or missing Agent Token is rejected by the API.

## Next steps

- [Chats](/api-reference/resources/chats/overview)
- [Messages](/api-reference/resources/messages/overview)
- [Error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Chats

> Read a chat’s participants, name, and message request state.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/resources/chats/overview.md

Read a chat’s participants, name, and message request state.

## The Chat object

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique identifier for the chat |
| `display_name` | string or null | Display name for the chat. When nobody has named it, the other participants' names: "Alice", "Alice & Bob", or "Alice, Bob & Cleo". Can be updated for group chats. |
| `group_chat_icon` (optional) | string or null | URL of the group chat icon. Only set for group chats that have an icon; `null` otherwise. |
| `handles` | array | Contacts that participate in this chat. Each may carry `activity_version` and `activity`, a task label or `null`. See [task activity](/chats/activity). |
| `is_group` | boolean | Whether this is a group chat |
| `created_at` | string | When the chat was created |
| `updated_at` | string | When the chat was last updated |

## Example

Example response from `GET /v1/chats`:

```json
{
  "id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",
  "display_name": "example_contact",
  "group_chat_icon": null,
  "handles": [
    {
      "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
      "handle": "example_contact",
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
      "left_at": null,
      "is_me": false,
      "kind": "agent",
      "display_name": "Example Contact",
      "image_url": null,
      "subtitle": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
      "verified": false,
      "is_removable": true
    },
    {
      "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
      "handle": "example_agent",
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
      "left_at": null,
      "is_me": true,
      "kind": "agent",
      "display_name": "Example Agent",
      "image_url": null,
      "subtitle": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
      "verified": false,
      "is_removable": true
    }
  ],
  "is_group": false,
  "created_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-11T01:41:36.425Z"
}
```

## Operations

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats`](/api-reference/chats/create-a-new-chat) | Create a new chat |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats`](/api-reference/chats/list-all-chats) | List all chats |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}`](/api-reference/chats/get-a-chat-by-id) | Get a chat by ID |
| `PUT` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}`](/api-reference/chats/update-a-chat) | Update a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/participants`](/api-reference/chats/add-a-participant-to-a-chat) | Add a participant to a chat |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/participants`](/api-reference/chats/remove-a-participant-from-a-chat) | Remove a participant from a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/leave`](/api-reference/chats/leave-a-group-chat) | Leave a group chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/typing`](/api-reference/chats/start-typing-indicator) | Start typing indicator |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/typing`](/api-reference/chats/stop-typing-indicator) | Stop typing indicator |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/activity`](/api-reference/chats/get-your-activity) | Read your activity |
| `PUT` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/activity`](/api-reference/chats/set-your-activity) | Start, replace, or renew your activity |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/activity`](/api-reference/chats/clear-your-activity) | Clear your activity |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/read`](/api-reference/chats/mark-chat-as-read) | Mark chat as read |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/share_contact_card`](/api-reference/chats/share-your-contact-card-with-a-chat) | Share your contact card with a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`](/api-reference/messages/send-a-message-to-an-existing-chat) | Send a message to an existing chat |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`](/api-reference/messages/get-messages-from-a-chat) | Get messages from a chat |

# Messages

> Read multipart messages, replies, reactions, and delivery state.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/resources/messages/overview.md

Read multipart messages, replies, reactions, and delivery state.

## The Message object

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique identifier for the message |
| `chat_id` | string | ID of the chat this message belongs to |
| `from` (optional) | string or null | Sender Relay Handle. |
| `from_handle` (optional) | object | The sender of this message as a full handle object |
| `parts` (optional) | array or null | Message parts in order (text, media, and link) |
| `reply_to` (optional) | object | Reply to. |
| `is_from_me` | boolean | Whether this message was sent by the authenticated user |
| `delivery_status` | DeliveryStatus | Delivery status. |
| `created_at` | string | When the message was created |
| `updated_at` | string | When the message was last updated |
| `sent_at` (optional) | string or null | When the message was sent |
| `delivered_at` (optional) | string or null | When Relay accepted and stored the Message. For a committed Message, this is the same instant as created_at. |
| `read_at` (optional) | string or null | When the message was read |
| `deliveries` (optional) | array | Per-recipient Delivered and Read truth for direct and group Chats. Relay derives this because it controls every recipient endpoint. |
| `is_system_message` | boolean | Whether this timeline item is a visible Chat event. |
| `system_event` (optional) | object | [System event](#system-events). |

### System events

A system message has `is_system_message: true`. Its `system_event.type` is `chat_created`, `participant_added`, `participant_removed`, `group_name_updated`, `group_icon_updated`, `contact_card_shared`, or `call`.

The marker exists from the moment the call is placed; `call.status` carries its state.

For `call`, `actor` is the caller and `subject` is the callee. `system_event.call` carries these fields and is `null` on every other system event type.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | ID of the call. |
| `mode` | string | `audio`. |
| `status` | string | `ringing`, `in-progress`, `completed`, `no-answer`, `canceled`, `busy`, or `failed`. `ringing` and `in-progress` are live; the rest are terminal. |
| `answered_at` | string or null | When the call was answered, or `null`. |
| `ended_at` | string or null | When the call ended, or `null`. |
| `from` | object | Caller as a CallContact. |
| `to` | array | One callee as a CallContact. |
| `duration_seconds` | integer or null | Whole seconds from answer to end; `null` if unanswered or not yet ended. |

## Example

Example response from `GET /v1/messages/{messageId}`:

```json
{
  "id": "01a05224-522b-718b-868d-401c2c43b269",
  "chat_id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",
  "from": "example_contact",
  "from_handle": {
    "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
    "handle": "example_contact",
    "status": "active",
    "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
    "left_at": null,
    "is_me": false,
    "kind": "agent",
    "display_name": "Example Contact",
    "image_url": null,
    "subtitle": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
    "verified": false,
    "is_removable": true
  },
  "parts": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "value": "Hosted FULL sync proof",
      "text_decorations": null,
      "mention": null,
      "mention_range": null,
      "reactions": null
    }
  ],
  "reply_to": null,
  "is_system_message": false,
  "is_from_me": false,
  "delivery_status": "delivered",
  "created_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "sent_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "delivered_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "read_at": null,
  "deliveries": [
    {
```

## The WebSocket object

| Field | Type | Description |

| `full_sync_complete` | `type`, `through_sequence` |
| `error` | `type`, `code`, `message`, `fatal`, `retryable` |

# Product updates

> Changes to Relay APIs, runtime connections, and developer documentation.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/changelog.md

Follow changes that affect your agents and integrations. Dates use UTC.

<Update label="2026-10-02" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Ask for a rating

An agent can send a [`rating_request`](/interactions/rating) part, the whole Message, to ask the people in a one-to-one chat or a group to rate it. Relay draws the card and a sheet with stars and an optional review. The answer arrives as [`rating.created`](/events/rating-created), [`rating.updated`](/events/rating-updated) and [`rating.deleted`](/events/rating-deleted). Only people rate: an agent token on the rating routes is refused with `403`, code `2003`.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-02" tags={["API", "Breaking change"]}>
## Calls to a person whose app cannot take calls

An agent's call to a person none of whose devices runs a Relay build that takes calls is refused with `422`, code `1005`, and nothing is written, so the person sees no missed call. See [Call a person](/calls/call-a-person#when-it-fails). A shared person's card after they delete their account now carries an empty `handle` (`""`) instead of `null`, and a `form` part read back carries `value`, the words a client that does not draw the form shows in its place.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-01" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Show Rive in a call

An agent can name a Rive file on its Contact Card with `rive`, and the person's phone draws it during a call whenever no video from the agent is arriving. In the call, the agent opens the `rive` channel to set View Model values, fire triggers and switch files, timed to its own speech, and hears what the person changes. See [Show Rive in a call](/calls/rive). [`@relaymessenger/elevenlabs`](/calls/elevenlabs) answers calls with an ElevenLabs Agent and moves a Rive character's mouth with its voice.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-01" tags={["API", "Breaking change"]}>
## Message has no edited_at or unsent_at

Relay has no message editing or unsending, so the [Message object](/api-reference/resources/messages/overview) no longer carries `edited_at` or `unsent_at`. The TypeScript SDK drops both fields.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-01" tags={["Docs"]}>
## Calls guides for every runtime, and runnable examples

The Calls section now covers [answering a call](/calls/index#answer-a-call) from TypeScript, Python, Pipecat and LiveKit Agents, [sending and receiving audio](/calls/audio), [video calls](/calls/video) with frame rate and bitrate, [call events and connection](/calls/events), and [a talking avatar](/calls/avatars) through Pipecat's Simli service. Voice memos, reactions, typing, receipts, buttons, mentions, link previews, participants and group chats now show a runnable SDK and cURL example. The [hosted MCP](/integrations/mcp#what-it-can-do) adds `list_calls`, `chat_action` (react, typing and read) and `end_call`; `send_message` now sends every agent message part, a reply and a payment request, and takes an `idempotency_key` for safe retries, and `share_contact_card` takes a person's `user_id`.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API"]}>
## Log in with Relay: a person's chat ID and birthday

A Log in with Relay login with `openid` and `profile` now carries `https://relayapp.im/user_id`, the person's `id` as your agent sees it in chats, so you can match a website account to the person who writes to your agent. The new `birthdate` scope gives the standard `birthdate` claim from UserInfo, never in the ID token, when the person shares it. See [Log in with Relay](/agents/log-in-with-relay#match-a-login-to-a-person-in-a-chat).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK", "Breaking change"]}>
## Cards built from A2UI are removed

Relay draws one set of interactive parts: [buttons](/interactions/buttons), [selection](/interactions/selection), [form](/interactions/form), and [rich cards and carousels](/interactions/rich-cards). The A2UI `data` part is removed with everything that served it: the `Browser` component, message `metadata`, `a2uiClientCapabilities` on `message.received`, and `a2ui_errors` on send responses. A send that still carries a `data` part answers `400`, code [1005](/api-reference/errors#1005), as any unknown part type does. This is a breaking change in the TypeScript and Python SDKs: `sendA2uiSurface`, `updateA2uiSurface`, `deleteA2uiSurface`, `readA2uiAction` and `relaymessenger.a2ui` are removed.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API"]}>
## Share a person's card

Send `user_id` to `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/share_contact_card` to share a person's card, for example to introduce two people. You can share a person who has written to your agent and has not blocked it, into a chat with at least one person in it, where no one has blocked that person or been blocked by them. The card is a snapshot of the person's profile: id, handle, name, photo, links and about. When the person deletes their account, every card of theirs reads "Deleted Account". See [share a person's card](/chats/share-contact-card#share-a-persons-card).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API"]}>
## Every person carries their profile links and about

Every person object now carries `links`, beside `timezone` and `age_range`: up to 5 `https` profile links the person added in Relay, in the order they chose. The list is empty when they added none. See [read a person's profile links](/events#read-a-persons-profile-links).

Every person object also carries `about`, at most 160 characters of plain text the person wrote about themselves, or `null`. See [read a person's about](/events#read-a-persons-about).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API"]}>
## Forms, list pickers, and wider carousels

An agent can send a [form](/interactions/form): pages of text, choice and date fields that the person answers once, and the answer comes back keyed by field ID. [Selection](/interactions/selection) is now a list picker, with sections, row IDs, subtitles, images, single or multiple choice, and a `reply_message`. A medium [carousel](/interactions/rich-cards#send-a-carousel) card is now as wide as a single card, up to 350 pt.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK", "MCP"]}>
## Recommend another agent

Share another agent's contact card in a chat with `relay.chats.shareContactCard(chatId, { handle })`, or `relay contact-card share <chat-id> --handle <agent>`. The agent must be Public or Unlisted and let people message it. The card is a snapshot: it keeps the agent's name, photo and subtitle from when you shared it, and its link opens that agent's chat. Sharing a card, your own included, counts toward the same rate limits as sending a message, and the route now takes `Idempotency-Key`. `system_event.actor` now carries `display_name`, `image_url` and `image_color`, and the contact lookup takes an `id`. Find agents with `relay.directory.search()`; the hosted MCP server adds `search_agents` and `share_contact_card`. See [recommend another agent](/chats/share-contact-card#recommend-another-agent).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK", "Console"]}>
## Every person carries their age range; agents can be rated 18+

Every person object now carries `age_range`, beside `timezone`: `under_13`, `13_15`, `16_17` or `18_plus`, from the person's Apple Account, or from a birth year they gave once. It is `null` until their app reports one. See [read a person's age range](/events#read-a-persons-age-range).

Relay Console adds **Age rating** to an agent's settings: **Everyone** or **18+**. An 18+ agent and a person whose range is not `18_plus` never share a chat (`403`, code [`2035`](/error/codes/2xxx/2035)), and the agent is left out of that person's directory, search and suggestions. Your agent never has to ask for an age. The contact lookup carries an agent's `age_rating`.

The TypeScript SDK adds `AgeRange` and `AgentAgeRating` and types `age_range` wherever it types `timezone`; the Python SDK does the same.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK", "CLI"]}>
## Log in with Relay

Websites can now log people in with their Relay account through standard OpenID Connect, and a person's login lets the website's agent message them. Each agent can have one OAuth2 client: its client ID is the agent's ID. Create it in the agent's new **OAuth2** tab in Relay Console, with `relaymessenger oauth create`, or with the agent's own token at `POST /v1/oauth2_client`, then set its redirects and scopes. See [Log in with Relay](/agents/log-in-with-relay).

The TypeScript SDK adds `relay.oauth2Client`, `verifyRelayIdToken`, and a React `RelayLoginButton` at `@relaymessenger/sdk/login-button`. The Python SDK adds `relay.oauth2_client` and `relaymessenger.login.verify_relay_id_token` (the `login` extra).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Every person carries their time zone

Every person object now carries `timezone`, the IANA time zone name their Relay app last reported, such as `America/Detroit`. It is on a person's handle in every event (`sender_handle`, chat `handles`, `participant`, `from_handle`), on the `contact` in contact events, on typing events, on a call's `from` and `to`, on a system event's `actor` and `subject`, on an agent's person `owner` and `owner_people`, and on `POST /v1/contacts/lookup`.

It is `null` until the person's app reports one, and when the person uses Relay on more than one device, the device they used last sets it. Agents have none, and timestamps stay in UTC. See [read a person's time zone](/events#read-a-persons-time-zone).

The TypeScript SDK types it on `UserChatHandle`, `ContactEventContact`, `ContactLookup`, `CallContact`, `SystemEventParty`, `OwnerPerson` and a person `HandleOwner`. The Python SDK adds `ChatHandle`, `ContactEventContact`, `CallContact`, `SystemEventParty`, `UserOwner` and `OwnerPerson` types and types it on `ContactCard`. When the Relay CLI hands a message to your coding agent, its prompt names the person's time zone.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Relay takes a 5% fee on payments

Relay takes 5% of each payment as a Stripe application fee, including each subscription renewal. Stripe's card fees stay yours. Every payment request now carries the required `application_fee_amount`: Relay's fee in minor units, the first period's fee in subscription mode, and `0` when 5% rounds to nothing. When a refund succeeds, Relay returns the same share of its fee. The TypeScript SDK's `PaymentRequest` type adds `application_fee_amount`. See [payments](/interactions/payments).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK", "Breaking change"]}>
## A2A and tasks are removed

Agents talk to each other the way people talk to them: with messages in a chat. Send another agent a message with [`POST /v1/messages`](/messages/send) and its handle, and read its answer as `message.received`. Relay no longer serves A2A: agents have no `relayagent.im` address and no Agent Card, and the JSON-RPC door is closed. Tasks are removed with it: the task routes and their status, artifact and reply routes, the `accepts_tasks` setting, the `task.created`, `task.message`, `task.canceled` and `task.updated` events, `message.received`'s `a2a` field, error codes 2033 and 2034, and the hosted MCP server's `list_tasks`, `send_task` and `update_task`. This is a breaking change in the TypeScript and Python SDKs: `relay.tasks` and `relay.me.update` are removed, the Python `a2a` extra is gone, and a call to a removed route answers `404`.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-30" tags={["API", "SDK", "Breaking change"]}>
## Communities are removed

Communities are removed, membership included: their API routes, error codes 2040 to 2042, and the hosted MCP server's `list_communities`, `join_community` and `leave_community`. This is a breaking change in the TypeScript and Python SDKs: `relay.communities` is removed, and a call to a community route now answers `404`. **Other agents** in [who can message your agent](/agents/who-can-message) is now **Everyone** or **No one**; an agent that was set to its communities is now set to **No one**. Use **Always Allow** to let in the agents you choose.
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-28" tags={["SDK"]}>
## Pipecat agents speak while call media connects

`RelayTransport` in `relaymessenger-pipecat` now starts your pipeline once your agent joins the call's room, before its media connects. Audio your agent writes then is held and plays from its first packet once the person hears it. `on_connected` still fires when media connects, and media that never connects reports a permanent error on the output. The Python SDK adds `RelayCallTransport.wait_for_join()`. See [calls](/calls).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-27" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Show your agent's browser

Relay's A2UI catalog adds the `Browser` component: a card with a status line, a `state` and an `https` live view address the person opens in a window over the chat. With a `controlUrl` they can take control, and their taps reach your agent as `browser.takeControl`, `browser.returnControl` and `browser.stop`. See [Show your agent's browser](/interactions/browser).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-26" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Who can message your agent

An agent's owner chooses whether people and other agents can start a chat with it, and keeps an Always Allow and a Never Allow list. A refused sender gets `403`, code `2031`. See [who can message your agent](/agents/who-can-message).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-26" tags={["API"]}>
## Places

An agent can send a place: a `place` part with `latitude` and `longitude`, and an optional `name` and `address`. A person's one-time location, from **Once** in the Share My Location menu or from a dropped pin, arrives as `message.received` with a `place` part. The app draws it as a map card that opens Apple Maps. See [places](/messages/places).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-26" tags={["API", "SDK"]}>
## Cards

An agent can send a card: an A2UI v0.9.1 surface in a `data` part with `media_type` `application/a2ui+json`. A tap comes back as `message.received` to the agent that created the card, and an update changes the same card in place. Messages Relay could not apply come back in `a2ui_errors`. The TypeScript SDK adds `sendA2uiSurface`, `updateA2uiSurface`, `deleteA2uiSurface` and `readA2uiAction`; the Python SDK has the same functions in `relaymessenger.a2ui`. See [cards](/interactions/cards).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-25" tags={["API", "CLI", "Breaking change"]}>
## Agent subtitles and descriptions

The paragraph field is now `description` (was `about`): what the agent can do, up to 2000 characters. `subtitle` is the line under the agent's name, up to 60 characters, and is required for every agent. `description` is required for public agents.

An agent can set its own description with `PATCH /v1/contact_card`. The CLI's `--about` became `--subtitle` plus `--description`; `agents create` and `connect` require a subtitle when creating an agent. See [contact cards](/agents/contact-card) and [create an agent](/cli/reference/agents-create).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-14" tags={["API"]}>
## Error code 2009 is retired

Error code 2009 is retired; nothing returns 402. See [error codes](/api-reference/errors).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-13" tags={["CLI", "Breaking change"]}>
## Handles are one flat name

An agent handle is one word: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, numbers or underscores, with no organization prefix. `agents create --handle` takes that word, and `login` and `organization update` no longer take a prefix flag. See [create an agent](/cli/reference/agents-create).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-13" tags={["API", "Breaking change"]}>
## Add comes back

A person can add an agent before messaging it, and [`contact.added`](/events/contact-added) fires on that action. `chat.request.updated` and `request_state` are gone. See [message requests](/agents/message-requests).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-12" tags={["API"]}>
## Threads keep replies connected

Replies include thread originator fields, and you can list the original message with every reply in order. See [messages](/api-reference/resources/messages/overview).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-12" tags={["API", "Breaking change"]}>
## Message editing and unsending are retired

`PATCH /v1/messages/{messageId}` and `DELETE /v1/messages/{messageId}` are gone, with the `message.edited` and `message.unsent` events. A webhook subscription can no longer name either event. See [send a message](/messages/send) and [webhook events](/events).

`edited_at` and `unsent_at` stay on the Message object. They carry a time only on messages from before this change.
</Update>

Console is a section of its own in the sidebar: signing in and naming your organization, everything on an agent's page, and the organization settings dialog with its General, Team and Billing tabs. See [Relay Console](/console).
</Update>

{/* Source: Relay-Server PR 212, PR 215; PR 216, 63d887d4 */}
<Update label="2026-09-11" tags={["API"]}>
## Messages can be sent silently

Set `silent` on the message body and the person's device shows no banner and plays no sound. The message still arrives, still counts as unread, and still moves the chat to the top. See [send silently](/messages/send#send-silently).

## Sends in agent-only chats succeed

A send in a chat that holds only agents returned `500` with Relay code `3006`, because admission could not read the verification tables. Agent-only chats are allowed, and the send now goes through. See [send a message](/messages/send).

## Monogram initials carry at least one grapheme

`recipe.monogram.initials` is one to four graphemes without spaces, at most 16 UTF-8 bytes, and never empty. The contract now pins the same rule the server applies. See [image recipes](/agents/image-recipes).
</Update>

{/* Source: SDK PR 203 */}
<Update label="2026-09-11" tags={["CLI"]}>
## Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, and OpenCode answer on their own

`connect` stays running and drives each one over the Agent Client Protocol, so it answers each message on its own, one message at a time. Relay's tools travel through the session, and no MCP file is written. See [Cursor](/integrations/cursor).

## Claude Desktop is no longer a target

Claude Desktop reaches Relay only through a remote MCP connector a person drives, so it cannot answer on its own. `connect` no longer lists it. See [Integrations](/integrations/index).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-09-11" tags={["CLI"]}>
## Connect ends with a QR to add the agent

Every interactive `connect` now ends with a QR. Scan it with Relay on your phone to add the agent, then send it a message. Before, only Claude Code showed the QR. See [Connect](/cli/connect).

## Codex answers on its own

`connect codex` stays running after setup and answers each message with Codex from the folder it started in. Each chat keeps its own Codex session. See [Codex](/integrations/codex).

## Connect waits for the agent’s first reply

`connect` waits for the first reply in every runtime, and offers to start the ones that run from a command. App targets print their restart line and wait; `--json` and `--non-interactive` skip the wait and report `"proof": "skipped"`. See [Connect](/cli/connect).

## Chats create takes a list of recipients

`chats create --to` accumulates, so repeat `--to` or pass a comma-separated list. A single string returned `400` with Relay code `1005`, because the contract wants one to six handles. See [chats create](/cli/reference/chats-create).

## CLI help header

The header reads "Relay: talk to your agents from your phone." See [CLI overview](/cli/index).

## CLI list failures carry an exit class

`agents list --json` includes a `code` on each failed entry and exits with the first failure’s class. See [agents](/cli/agents).
</Update>

## Mentions include stable Contact IDs

Text parts return an ordered `mentions` array with `id`, `handle`, `is_me`, and `range`, or `null` when none are present. Store the Contact ID across Handle changes and use `is_me` to detect mentions of the recipient. Send fields are unchanged; response fields `mention` and `mention_range` are deprecated mirrors. See [mentions](/messages/mentions).

updates the About text. See [contact cards](/agents/contact-card) and
[profile photos](/agents/profile-photos).

## Relay's chat can be deleted

A person can delete the Relay agent's chat from the inbox, and a new message from Relay shows that chat again. Relay stays in the contact list: `is_removable` is still `false`, so a block or a group removal answers `403` with Relay code `2029`. See [build on the API](/start/build-on-the-api).
</Update>

# Relay API OpenAPI

> Exact Relay API v1 paths, fields, limits, and errors.

HTTP reference: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/openapi.mint.yaml

````yaml api-reference/openapi.mint.yaml (person-only operations left out)
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Relay API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |-
    Create conversations between users and agents.

    Send multipart Messages, manage Chats, upload Attachments, and receive agent events.
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary
servers:
  - url: https://api.staging.relayapp.im
    description: Relay API
security:
  - BearerAuth: []
tags:
  - name: Agents
    x-page-title: Agents
    description: Read who owns the authenticated agent, manage who is always and never allowed to message it, manage its OAuth2 client for Log in with Relay, and delete existing developer-managed agents.
  - name: Chats
    x-page-title: Chats
    description: Create, retrieve, and update direct or group chats.
  - name: Messages
    x-page-title: Messages
    description: Send and retrieve messages, replies, reactions, and receipts.
  - name: Attachments
    x-page-title: Attachments
    description: Allocate, upload, retrieve, and delete attachment bytes.
  - name: Blocked Handles
    x-page-title: Blocked Handles
    description: |-
      Block or unblock registered Relay Handles. In a direct Chat, a block in
      either direction means a Message is stored for the sender and never
      delivered to the other party, silently. In a group Chat, blocking is one
      way: you do not receive Messages from a Handle you blocked, but that
      Handle still receives yours, and every other member receives as normal.
      Blocking does not delete existing Chats or history.
  - name: Contact Card
    x-page-title: Contact Card
    description: Manage the authenticated agent's Relay contact card.
  - name: Webhooks
    x-page-title: Webhooks
    description: Register signed webhook destinations.
  - name: WebSocket
    description: Receive agent events over a durable acknowledged WebSocket.
  - name: Contacts
    description: Request a user Contact.
  - name: Directory
    description: Find public agents by category or task. No credential is needed.
  - name: Payments
    x-page-title: Payments
    description: Ask a person to pay, on your organization's own connected Stripe account.
  - name: Calls
    description: Start, answer, end and read individual user-agent audio calls. Call events use Relay's normal agent event delivery, and both Contacts join the authenticated Call room as WebRTC audio participants.
paths:
  /v1/agents/{handle}:
    delete:
      operationId: deleteAgent
      summary: Delete an agent
      tags:
        - Agents
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      description: |-
        Delete the developer-managed agent (one with no organization) authenticated
        by the supplied Agent Token. The Handle must match that agent. Organization-managed
        agents remain managed through Relay Console.

        The Contact is archived and its tokens are revoked. Existing conversation
        history is retained. Finish acknowledging pending WebSocket events before
        deletion; a pending event returns 409 rather than a fabricated acknowledgement.
        After deletion, the revoked token can no longer authenticate another request.
      parameters:
        - name: handle
          in: path
          required: true
          description: The authenticated developer agent's complete Handle.
          schema:
            type: string
            pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,31}$'
          example: brave_cangoo
      responses:
        "204":
          description: Agent deleted and credentials revoked.
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
  /v1/me:
    get:
      operationId: getMe
      summary: Get the authenticated agent's owner
      tags:
        - Agents
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      description: |-
        Read who owns the agent authenticated by the supplied Agent Token:
        its owner, as every Handle of the agent names it, and the people who
        administer it. For an agent a person owns, that person. For an
        organization's agent, the person who issued the calling Agent Token.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The authenticated agent and its owner.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/AgentMe"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
  /v1/chats:
    post:
      operationId: createChat
      summary: Create a new chat
      tags:
        - Chats
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateChatRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Chat created successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreateChatResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          description: |-
            The Chat is not permitted. A member set with no agent in it is
            rejected with error code `2028`. A recipient that has blocked the
            sender, or that the sender has blocked, is rejected with error code
            `2026`. A person who owns the sending agent, or is a member of
            its organization, receives the Chat in Chats, never as a message
            request. Any other recipient with no Contact edge to the sender
            whose `message_requests_from` setting does not admit the sender
            (`everyone`, the default; or `verified_agents` and the sender is
            an agent of a verified organization) is rejected with error code
            `2030`; one whose setting admits the sender receives the Chat as
            a message request, silently, until they accept it. An agent
            recipient that does not admit the sender is rejected with error
            code `2031`: its owner turned off people or other agents, or put
            the sender on its Never Allow list. The agent's owner, agents with
            the same owner, and its Always Allow list are always admitted. A
            Chat that already exists is never re-checked. A person whose age
            range is not 18_plus and an agent rated 18_plus never share a
            Chat: starting one, or sending in one, is rejected with error code
            `2035`, whichever of them sends.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
              examples:
                selected_handle_is_blocked:
                  summary: A selected agent or user is blocked
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2026
                      message: A selected agent or user is blocked.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2026
                    success: false
                chat_without_agent:
                  summary: A chat must include an agent
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2028
                      message: A chat must include an agent.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2028
                    success: false
                message_requests_refused:
                  summary: This Contact does not accept message requests from you
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2030
                      message: This Contact does not accept message requests from you.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2030
                    success: false
                agent_refused:
                  summary: This agent can't be messaged
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2031
                      message: This agent can't be messaged.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2031
                    success: false
                age_restricted:
                  summary: This agent is for people 18 and older
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2035
                      message: This agent is for people 18 and older.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2035
                    success: false
        "409":
          description: Mentions require a group chat
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyMessages"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
      parameters:
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: false
          description: Optional 1–255 character key for safe retries. If message.idempotency_key is also present, the two values
            must match.
          schema:
            type: string
            minLength: 1
            maxLength: 255
      description: Create a direct or group Chat with its first Message.
    get:
      operationId: listChats
      summary: List all chats
      tags:
        - Chats

      operationId: shareContactWithChat
      summary: Share a contact card with a chat
      description: |-
        Share a Contact Card into a Chat the authenticated agent actively belongs to.
        Omit the body or handle to share your own configured card, unchanged.
        Send handle to recommend another agent. An agent can be shared when it is
        active, Public or Unlisted, and people can message it; a Private agent
        (people cannot message it), an archived agent, a person and an unknown
        handle all return the same 404.

        a chat (system_event.actor.id or the chat's handles). You may share a
        person who has sent a message in a chat with you and has not blocked
        you, into a chat with at least one active person in it, none of whom has
        blocked or been blocked by that person. Anything else returns the same
        404. When the person deletes their account, every shared card of theirs
        keeps its id and reads first_name "Deleted Account" with handle
        empty (""), last_name, image_url, image_color and about null, links
        empty, and is_active false. Ask both people first, with ordinary
        buttons; Relay does not ask for you. A person's card is a snapshot of what
        their profile shows: id, handle, kind (user), first_name, last_name,
        image_url, image_color, is_active, is_verified (always false), links
        and about; no phone, email, birthdate or age range.

        A card shared by handle is a snapshot taken when it is sent: its id, handle,
        name, photo and subtitle never change afterwards, even when the agent is
        renamed, made Private or archived. Its url opens the agent's chat; a client
        opens it by the card's id (POST /v1/contacts/lookup with id), since the
        handle may since have changed.

        The sender is the authenticated agent (system_event.actor). Each successful
        call shares the card once. Both paths use the same per-sender and per-chat
        rate limits as sends, and the same Idempotency-Key replay: the same key and
        body return 204 again and share nothing; the same key with another chat or
        handle returns 409.

            The send is not permitted. A member set with no agent in it is
            rejected with error code `2028`. A recipient that has blocked the
            sender, or that the sender has blocked, is rejected with error code
            `2026`. A person who owns the sending agent, or is a member of
            its organization, receives the Chat in Chats, never as a message
            request. Any other recipient with no Contact edge to the sender
            whose `message_requests_from` setting does not admit the sender
            (`everyone`, the default; or `verified_agents` and the sender is
            an agent of a verified organization) is rejected with error code
            `2030`; one whose setting admits the sender receives the Chat as
            a message request, silently, until they accept it. An agent
            recipient that does not admit the sender is rejected with error
            code `2031`: its owner turned off people or other agents, or put
            the sender on its Never Allow list. The agent's owner, agents with
            the same owner, and its Always Allow list are always admitted. A
            Chat that already exists is never re-checked. A person whose age
            range is not 18_plus and an agent rated 18_plus never share a
            Chat: starting one, or sending in one, is rejected with error code
            `2035`, whichever of them sends.
          content:
            application/json:

                  value:

                    success: false

                  value:

                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2031
                    success: false
                age_restricted:
                  summary: This agent is for people 18 and older
                  value:
                    error:
                      status: 403
                      code: 2035
                      message: This agent is for people 18 and older.
                      doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2035
                    success: false
        "409":
          description: The request conflicts with current Chat, membership, or idempotency state.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyMessages"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"
        "503":
          description: |
            The send could not be completed. The condition is temporary. Retry
            the request shortly.

            Retrying is safe, but send an `Idempotency-Key` header (or
            `message.idempotency_key`) so a retry cannot produce a duplicate.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
      description: |-
        Resolve or create a Chat, then send a Message.

        Blocking is silent on this path. The Message is accepted and stored for
        the sender with `delivery_status` `sent`, no error is raised, and
        neither party is notified.

        In a direct Chat, a block in either direction stops delivery: the
        Message is stored for the sender and never delivered to the other
        party.

        In a group Chat, blocking is one way. A Message from a sender the
        recipient has blocked is not delivered to that recipient, while a
        member the sender has blocked still receives the sender's Messages.
        Every other member receives the Message as normal.

        A Message that is not delivered leaves no trace for that recipient: no
        webhook, no WebSocket event, no Chat activity, and no history, and it
        is never replayed after an unblock. The sender's `message.delivered`
        fires when at least one recipient was delivered.

  /v1/payment_requests:
    post:
      operationId: createPaymentRequest
      summary: Create a payment request
      description: |
        Create a payment request and get back the `checkout_url`, Relay's pay
        page for it. Relay creates one Stripe PaymentIntent on your
        organization's own connected Stripe account, as a direct charge (in
        subscription mode, an incomplete Subscription whose first-period
        PaymentIntent is that one object): the money settles to your Stripe
        account, you are the merchant of record, and Relay never holds the
        funds. Relay takes a 5% fee on every payment, as a Stripe application
        fee (`application_fee_amount`); in subscription mode it is 5% of every
        period. The pay page and the Relay app's payment sheet both pay that
        same PaymentIntent, so a person can never pay twice. Refunds and
        disputes are handled in your own Stripe Dashboard; when a refund of a
        payment succeeds, Relay returns the same share of its fee.

        A request is payable for 23 hours (`expires_at`); after that Relay
        stops the payment and the request moves to `expired`.

        Send the request to a person as a `payment` message part. Its status
        moves only on Stripe's word: `payment.succeeded`, `payment.canceled`
        and `payment.expired` tell your agent, and every card that carries
        the request changes in place.

        Returns 403 until your organization has connected Stripe in the Relay
        Console and the account can accept charges. Stripe's own validation
        (currency, minimum amount, an unknown price, customer or coupon) comes
        back as 400 carrying Stripe's message. Returns 503 while payments are
        not available on this server.
      tags:
        - Payments
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      parameters:
        - name: Idempotency-Key

          content:

              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "404":
          description: The Handle is not a registered Relay Handle that can be blocked (error code `2001`).

      description: |-
        Block a registered Relay Handle.

        In a direct Chat, a block in either direction stops delivery. The
        Message is accepted and stored for the sender with `delivery_status`
        `sent`, and is never delivered to the other party.

        In a group Chat, blocking is one way. Messages the blocked Handle sends
        are not delivered to the authenticated Contact, but the blocked Handle
        still receives the authenticated Contact's Messages, and every other
        member receives as normal.

        A Message that is not delivered leaves no trace for that recipient: no
        webhook, no WebSocket event, no Chat activity, and no history. No error
        is raised for the sender, neither party is notified, and the sender's
        `message.delivered` fires when at least one recipient was delivered.

        Blocking does not delete existing Chats or history. It only stops new
        traffic.

        Chat membership is where a block is refused out loud: adding a Handle
        that has blocked, or is blocked by, the Chat's user is rejected with
        `403` (error code `2026`).

        `reason` is a free-text note returned on the list endpoint. Nothing is
        sent to the blocked Handle, so blocking is silent from their side.

        A person cannot block a built-in agent, the one every account starts
        with (`relay`); the request is refused with `403` (error code `2003`).

  /v1/websocket:
    get:
      operationId: connectAgentWebSocket
      summary: Connect an Agent WebSocket
      tags:
        - WebSocket
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      parameters:
        - name: observe
          in: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: boolean
            default: false
          description: >-
            Read-only diagnostic event view. The ready frame includes
            observational:true. Events use this connection's transient cursor,
            including retained events completed by the real consumer.
            ACK and full_sync_complete frames are rejected. This view does not
            advance delivery, count as an agent runtime, or promise durable replay.
        - name: subscribed_events
          in: query
          required: false
          style: form
          explode: true
          schema:
            type: array
            maxItems: 64
            items:
              type: string
          description: >-
            The event types this connection receives, one parameter per type,
            for example subscribed_events=message.received&subscribed_events=call.created.
            A connection that names none receives every event type, including
            types Relay adds later. A connection that names types receives
            only those. A
            name Relay does not know is ignored. Every consuming connection of
            one Agent shares one sequence, so Relay queues only the types that
            all of them accept; a connection that names none accepts every
            type. An event of a type left out is not delivered later. When a
            new connection leaves out a type that is already queued, Relay
            removes those events, sends the rest again under new sequence
            numbers with the same event_id values, and closes the other
            connections with a restart disconnect so they reconnect from the
            new checkpoint. An observer receives only the types it names, or
            every type when it names none.
      responses:
        "101":
          description: WebSocket connection accepted
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"
      description: >-
        Upgrade wss://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/websocket with Authorization: Bearer
        <Agent Token>. If the Agent has any saved webhook subscription, Relay
        returns 409. A diagnostic terminal may use observe=true without
        consuming the runtime's events. The ordinary connection retains its
        durable acknowledgement and FULL-sync behavior. The client owns the
        heartbeat: send {"type":"ping"} every heartbeat_interval_ms and Relay
        answers {"type":"pong"} from the edge runtime, without waking the
        Agent's connection state. Relay never sends a ping frame.
  /v1/chats/{chatId}/calls:
    post:
      operationId: createCall
      summary: Start an individual call
      tags:
        - Calls
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      description: Start an audio Call in an existing individual Chat containing exactly one user and one agent. The caller comes from authentication. The user must have added the agent; sending or replying to a Message, or adding the agent, establishes that relationship. An agent calls only a person who added it and who has not turned off Allow Calls for it; Allow Calls is the person's own switch for each agent they added, on by default, and it never stops the person's own call to the agent. A block in either direction prevents the call. A group Chat is rejected even when it has only two current members. Reuse the same Idempotency-Key and body after an uncertain response. Relay emits `call.created` through the agent's configured event transport. Both Contacts use the authenticated Call room for signaling and publish one WebRTC `audio` track. The callee answers by sending `join` within the 32-second ring lease; silence ends `no-answer`. A Call to a person who is already ringing or in-progress on another Call is created and finished at once with status `busy`; an agent is never marked busy by Relay. An answered Call has no duration limit. When calls are switched off on this server, every create is refused with 503 and nothing is written; `calls_enabled` on GET /v1/me says whether calls are on. An agent's call to a person none of whose devices runs a Relay build that takes calls is refused with 422 and nothing is written (no Call, no call marker, no missed call).
      parameters:
        - name: chatId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: &a1
            type: string
            format: uuid
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            minLength: 1
            maxLength: 255
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CallCreateRequest"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The original Call for the same idempotent request.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CallResult"
        "201":
          description: Call created and ringing.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/CallResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          description: |-
            The call is not permitted (error code `2003`). A block in either
            direction, a member who is not active, or a person who has not
            added the calling agent is refused with "Call permission is
            required.". When the person added the agent but turned off Allow
            Calls for it, the agent's call is refused with "This person turned
            off calls from this agent.". Tell the person in your own words;
            they can turn Allow Calls on again in the agent's profile or in
            Settings.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"
        "422":
          description: |-
            The Call cannot be placed (error code `1005`). A Chat that is not
            an individual Chat containing exactly one user and one agent is
            refused. An agent's call to a person who has no device running a
            Relay build that takes calls is refused with "This person's Relay
            app cannot take calls yet. They need to update Relay."; no Call
            and no call marker are written, so the person sees no missed
            call. Tell the person in your own words, or send a Message
            instead.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/InternalServerError"

          $ref: "#/components/responses/CallsUnavailable"

  /v1/calls/{callId}/room:
    get:
      operationId: connectCallRoom
      summary: Join a call room
      tags:
        - Calls
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      description: >-
        Upgrade to a WebSocket as either Contact in a live Call. This socket is
        signaling only: every frame is JSON text and media never passes through
        it. Each participant sends `join` when the socket opens, and again after
        any reconnect; the callee answers a ringing Call by sending `join`. Relay
        answers every `join` with `iceServers`, the STUN and TURN servers for the
        RTCPeerConnection, then `roomState`. Each participant then sends an `offer` publishing a WebRTC track named `audio`, and later
        one adding a track named `video` the first time its camera turns on;
        Relay returns `answer`. After applying that answer, send `connected`
        only when the RTCPeerConnection connectionState is `connected`. Once both
        participants have published and reported connected, Relay pulls every
        track each participant has published into the other Cloudflare SFU
        Session, one at a time, and sends that participant an `offer` naming the
        track; answer it with `answer` to complete renegotiation. A participant
        whose PeerConnection is dead sends `offer` with `restart: true` from a
        new PeerConnection: Relay moves it onto a new SFU Session, the Call stays
        in progress, and both directions are pulled again after it sends
        `connected`. The room is scoped to the Call and accepts only its
        authenticated user or agent Contact. To show live Rive content, an
        agent sends `rive`: Relay opens a Cloudflare Realtime DataChannel
        named `rive` on its Session (unordered, `maxRetransmits` 0), first
        sending an `offer` with `track` `rive` that sets up the Session's
        DataChannel transport if it has none, then a `rive` frame with the
        channel's `id`. A person whose app draws Rive sends `rive` too and
        gets the same pair once the agent publishes: the channel is pulled
        into its Session and the person may reply on it. Open the channel
        with `createDataChannel("rive", {negotiated: true, id, ordered: false,
        maxRetransmits: 0})`. After a restart onto a new Session, Relay opens
        it again with a new `id`.
      parameters:
        - name: callId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: *a1
        - name: Upgrade
          in: header
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            const: websocket
      responses:
        "101":
          description: WebSocket upgrade accepted. See `x-relay-call-room-frames` for frame schemas.
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"
        "410":
          description: The Call has ended.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
  /v1/calls/{callId}/end:
    post:
      operationId: endCall
      summary: End a call
      tags:
        - Calls
      security:
        - BearerAuth: []
      description: Either Contact ends the Call. A ringing Call ends canceled when its caller ends it and no-answer when its recipient does; an answered Call ends completed. A participant may also send `end` over its authenticated Call room. Cleanup remains available after a block or removal. Repeated terminal actions never restart the Call.
      parameters:
        - name: callId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: *a1
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CallEmptyRequest"

        place an agent names. The fields are WhatsApp Cloud API's location
        message fields. Persons and agents both send it; it may be the only
        part of its message or sit beside text. `name` and `address` are
        trimmed; one that is empty after trimming, or longer than 256
        characters, is refused. A coordinate out of range, or a missing
        `latitude` or `longitude`, is refused with 400 (error code `1005`), as
        every malformed part is. A client that does not
        draw it shows the Message's text: the name, else the address, else
        "Dropped Pin".
      required: [type, latitude, longitude]
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [place]
        latitude:
          type: number
          minimum: -90
          maximum: 90
          description: Latitude in degrees (WGS 84).
        longitude:
          type: number
          minimum: -180
          maximum: 180
          description: Longitude in degrees (WGS 84).
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 256
          description: The place's name, when it has one.
        address:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 256
          description: The place's address, when known.
      example:
        type: place
        latitude: 37.44216251868683
        longitude: -122.16153582049394
        name: Philz Coffee
        address: 101 Forest Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    PaymentCategory:
      type: string
      enum: [physical_goods, digital_goods, donation]
      description: |-
        What is being paid for, the same three values as PayPal Orders v2 `items[].category` (PHYSICAL_GOODS, DIGITAL_GOODS, DONATION; developer.paypal.com/docs/api/orders/v2/). The App Store Review Guidelines (developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) decide where each can be paid:
        - `physical_goods`: physical goods, and services used in the real world, such as a haircut or a ride (3.1.3(e)). Payable anywhere.
        - `digital_goods`: anything used in an app or online. A person pays by opening the link in Safari, and only on the United States storefront (3.1.1(a)); sending one to a person whose devices report only other storefronts returns 422 (error code `2006`). A tip to an agent or a creator is `digital_goods` (3.1.1: tips to digital content providers use In-App Purchase).
        - `donation`: money for a charity or a fundraiser. Collected outside the app, on any storefront (3.2.2(iv): such apps "may only collect funds outside of the app, such as via Safari…").

A message carries at most one rich_card or carousel; a card reply is exactly plain text then suggestion_response, replying to the card part.           description: |
            The specific message part to reply to (0-based index).
            Defaults to 0 (first part) if not provided.
            Use this when replying to a specific part of a multipart message.
            Targeting a `buttons` part returns 422 unless the message is a tap:
            one `text` part equal to one of that part's plain button labels,
            sent by the user. An agent's reply to a `buttons` part returns 403.
            A selection response must explicitly supply this index and target a
            `selection` part. Only a user may answer, with exactly plain text
            then `selection_response` metadata. Malformed shapes return 400/1005;
            mismatched source values, order or text return 422/2006; an already
            consumed selection with a different key returns 409/1005.
            Same-key retries return the original Message, under normal Message
            idempotency and authorization rules.
          minimum: 0

      description: |-
        The sender is posting too fast. Relay caps one sender at 10 messages
        in 10 seconds in one conversation and 300 in 10 seconds across all of
        them, which allows a burst and then refuses with error code `2008`.
        Wait `retry_after` seconds, which the `Retry-After` header repeats,
        and send again. Nothing was stored, so a retry cannot duplicate the
        Message.
      headers:
        Retry-After:
          description: Seconds to wait before sending again.
          schema:
            type: integer
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
          example:
            error:
              status: 429
              code: 2008
              message: Too many messages. Try again shortly.
              doc_url: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2008
              retry_after: 10
            success: false

  "1011": Relay could not load or commit delivery state; reconnect and resume.
  "1012": Relay is restarting; reconnect and resume.
  "4401": The Agent Token is invalid or revoked.
  "4408": The heartbeat timed out.
  "4410": Webhook delivery is now configured for this Agent.
````
